ITQAN:v2p549/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p549/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p549/r2.claim: When two things are named, the pronoun usually returns to the second: here إنها refers to prayer, though another view takes it as the implied act of seeking help.
ITQAN:v2p549/r2.anchor: فأعيد الضمير للصلاة وقيل للإستعانة المفهومة من ﴿ استعينوا ﴾

DAMGHANI:v1p271/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r8.claim: Al-ṣabr can mean fasting in the command to seek help through patience and prayer.
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r8.anchor: فوجه منها الصبر الصوم قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة يا ايها الذين آمنوا استعينوا بالصبر والصلاة يعني بالصبر والصوم

TABATABAI:12:18#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r3.claim: Jacob completes patience with trust in God, just as he later says he hopes God will bring his sons back together.
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r3.anchor: ولهذا كله لما قال يعقوب عليه السلام { فصبر جميل } عقبه بقوله { والله المستعان على ما تصفون }

BIQAI-FULL:v6p20/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p20/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p20/r1.claim: The sequence ‘patience and prayer’ in 2:45 differs because its addressees are unbelievers engrossed in worldly things, while Luqmān’s addressee is a believing ascetic.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p20/r1.anchor: واختلاف المخاطب في الموضعين أوجب اختلاف الترتيبين

BURSEVI:v1p97/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p97/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p97/r1.claim: Patience helps meet needs by waiting for deliverance and relief while relying on God, or by fasting, which restrains appetite and purifies the soul.
BURSEVI:v1p97/r1.anchor: بانتظار الظفر والفرج توكلا على الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v1p97/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p97/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p97/r2.claim: Prayer means turning to it and seeking refuge in it so that needs are granted and hardships repaired; these practices address the strain of relinquishing status and wealth.
BURSEVI:v1p97/r2.anchor: التوسل بالصلاة والالتجاء إليها حتى تجابوا

BURSEVI:v1p97/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p97/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p97/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet resorted to prayer whenever a matter distressed him.
BURSEVI:v1p97/r3.anchor: روي أنه عليه السلام "كان إذا حزبه أمر فزع إلى الصلاة"

BURSEVI:v1p97/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p97/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v1p97/r4.claim: When Ibn Abbas was told on a journey that his daughter had died, he praised God for the covering and relief, prayed beside the road, then returned to his mount reciting this verse.
BURSEVI:v1p97/r4.anchor: وروي أن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما نعي له بنت وهو في سفر فاسترجع

BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to seeking help through patience and prayer; this is heavy and difficult except for the humble, who are meek and fearful. Humility may be bodily with submission of heart, or lowered eyes with yielding limbs.
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r1.anchor: المخبتين الخائفين والخشوع بالجوارح والخضوع بالقلب

BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r2.claim: Prayer is not burdensome for the humble because absorption in intimate conversation with God makes them unaware of hardship; the Prophet called it the delight of his eye and treated worldly work as toil.
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r2.anchor: لأنهم يستغرقون في مناجاة ربهم فلا يدركون ما يجري عليهم من المشاق والمتاعب

BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r3.claim: In this context, zann means certainty though it can also mean doubt; the word raja can likewise mean security or fear, according to al-Kawashi.
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r3.anchor: يوقنون لأن الظن يكون يقينا ويكون شكا فهو من الأضداد

BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r7.claim: People without certainty about recompense, hope for reward, or fear of punishment experience only hardship, like hypocrites and ostentatious worshippers.
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r7.anchor: وأما الذين لا يوقنون بالجزاء ولا يرجون الثواب ولا يخافون العقاب

BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r8.claim: Patience in enduring harm and obedience is the struggle against the self, restraining it from desires and excess; it is characteristic of prophets and the righteous.
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r8.anchor: فالصبر على الأذى والطاعات من باب جهاد النفس وقمعها عن شهواتها

BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r9.speaker: يحيى بن اليمان
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r9.claim: Yahya ibn al-Yaman defines patience as not wishing for a state other than what God allotted and being content with His decree in worldly and afterlife matters; it is like the head to the body.
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r9.anchor: قال يحيى بن اليمان : الصبر أن لا تتمنى

BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r10.claim: A Persian couplet cited from Hafiz says stone can become ruby through patience, but only through the blood of the liver, emphasizing the cost of patient endurance.
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r10.anchor: كويند سنك لعل شود در مقام صبر

BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r11.claim: God gives ordinary good deeds tenfold, gives charity in His cause the multiplied reward of a grain producing seven ears, and gives the patient reward without measure while praising them.
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r11.anchor: وجعل أجر الصابرين بغير حساب ومدح أهله

BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r12.claim: A hadith calls God the most patient toward hurtful speech: people ascribe a child to Him, yet He continues to cure and provide them; divine patience here means forbearance, delaying deserved punishment.
BURSEVI:v1p97#2/r12.anchor: ووصف الله بالصبر إنما هو بمعنى الحلم وهو تأخير العقوبة عن المستحقين لها

BURSEVI:v1p98/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p98/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p98/r1.claim: The sinner feels less secure from punishment under the divine attribute Patient than under Forbearing.
BURSEVI:v1p98/r1.anchor: والفرق بين الحليم والصبور أن المذنب لا يأمن العقوبة في صفة الصبور

BURSEVI:v1p98/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p98/r2.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v1p98/r2.claim: A saying defines humility as treating noble and lowly people equally in justice and humbling oneself in every duty, not merely eating or wearing rough things; outward humility beyond inward humility is hypocrisy.
BURSEVI:v1p98/r2.anchor: وقيل في الخشوع أتريد أن تكون إماما للناس ولا تعرف الخشوع

BURSEVI:v1p98/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p98/r3.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
BURSEVI:v1p98/r3.claim: Sahl says true humility reaches every hair on the body; fear settled in the heart naturally makes the outward form humble, lowered, and respectful.
BURSEVI:v1p98/r3.anchor: قال سهل بن عبد الله لا تكون خاشعا حتى تخشع كل شعرة على جسدك

BURSEVI:v1p98/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p98/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p98/r4.claim: Earlier Muslims tried to conceal the outward signs of genuine humility; affected displays, staged weeping, and bowed heads to win esteem are blameworthy tricks of Satan and self-delusion.
BURSEVI:v1p98/r4.anchor: وأما المذموم فتكلفه والتباكي ومطأطأة الرأس كما يفعله الجهال

BURSEVI:v1p98/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p98/r5.speaker: عمر
BURSEVI:v1p98/r5.claim: As related in al-Qurtubi, Umar spoke loudly enough to be heard, walked quickly, and struck hard; the author presents this as genuine asceticism and humility rather than a staged display.
BURSEVI:v1p98/r5.anchor: وكان عمر رضي الله عنه إذا تكلم أسمع وإذا مشى أسرع وإذا ضرب أوجع

BURSEVI:v1p98/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p98/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p98/r6.claim: The Najmiyya reading takes patience as resisting the ego's desires and prayer as remaining at the threshold of the unseen and the Lord's presence.
BURSEVI:v1p98/r6.anchor: وقال في "التأويلات النجمية" : {واستعينوا بالصبر} عن شهوات النفس

BURSEVI:v1p98/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p98/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p98/r7.claim: In this inward reading, the humble are people whose secrets have received divine self-disclosure so their souls submit; manifestation brings intimacy with God and removes the burden from creation.
BURSEVI:v1p98/r7.anchor: وهم الذين تجلى الحق لأسرارهم فخشعت له أنفسهم

ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r18.claim: When these commands feel difficult, people should seek God's help through patience and prayer.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r18.anchor: ihtiyâcâtınıza sabr u salât ile isti‘âne ediniz.

ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r1.claim: Patience means enduring pain with perseverance and resistance; it is the key to relief and success and the first means of seeking God's help in hardship.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r1.anchor: “Sabır” acıya katlanmak, onu geçirmek için sebat ve mukavemet etmektir ki her ferahın, her muvaffakiyetin anahtarıdır.

ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r2.claim: Impatient souls remain distressed, fail to withstand events, crave everything, undervalue blessings, and collapse when even a little is lost.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r2.anchor: Sabırsız nefisler her zaman darlık içindedir. Onların hâdisât-ı kevniyeye hiç mukavemetleri yoktur.

ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r3.claim: Because worldly conditions always change, the afflicted should attach their hearts to God, trust that hardship will pass by His permission, and await His aid sincerely; they will ultimately be delivered.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r3.anchor: Allah’a rabt-ı kalb ederek bunun da bi-iznillâh geçeceğine iman eder ve Allah’ın inâyetini, felâh u ferah gününü hulûs-i kalb ve kemâl-i îmân içinde beklerse âkıbet halâs olur

ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r4.claim: People should train themselves in patience; fasting is the best way to habituate the self to patience and treat its addictions.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r4.anchor: Oruç insanı her hâlde sabra alıştırır, tiryakilikleri tedavi eder.

ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r5.claim: The verse's intended primary meaning is patience, though patience here has also been interpreted directly as fasting, which serves as a means to it.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r5.anchor: fakat her iki hâlde de burada maksûd-i aslî bizzat ma‘nâ-yı sabrdır.

ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r6.claim: Prayer is highly beneficial alongside patience: its ordered bodily and spiritual acts restore inner order, ease suffering, strengthen trust, and help people withstand hardship with happiness and dignity.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r6.anchor: bütün bunlar me‘ûnet-i ilâhiyenin celbine vâsıta olur. Darlıktan patlayacak dereceye gelen o fena nefisler kuvvetlerini, itimadlarını artırırlar

ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r7.claim: Human suffering fundamentally stems from public moral decline and the promotion of falsehood over truth, which brings divine anger, although God's mercy is universal.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r7.anchor: bütün dünyadaki ıztırâb-ı beşerînin esâsı ahlâk-ı umûmiyenin sukūtunda ve hak yerine bâtılın tervîcindedir. Gazab-ı ilâhîyi celbeden de budur.

ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r8.claim: Patience, prayer, and seeking help are difficult, but they do not burden humble, respectful people who reflect; these practices can become a pleasure and habit for them.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r8.anchor: başını önüne alıp düşünen saygılı kimselere ağır gelmez, hatta zevk verir, meleke olur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r1.speaker: Râgıb el-İsfahânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r1.claim: Raghib defines patience as enduring pain and hardship while trusting God, compelling oneself to required duties and away from forbidden conduct, and persisting toward a good goal.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r2.speaker: Gazzâlî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r2.claim: Ghazali defines patience broadly as the power of belief resisting selfish desires and passions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r2.anchor: Gazzâlî, sabrı “inanç gücünün bencil istek ve tutkulara karşı koyması” şeklinde oldukça kapsamlı bir ifadeyle tanımlar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r3.claim: Because unbelief also arises from a kind of belief, unbelievers' perseverance can be assessed in this sense, and patience's value varies with the nature of the belief behind it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r3.anchor: İnkârcılık da bir tür inançtan kaynaklandığı için inkârcılarda görülen sabrı da bu anlamda değerlendirmek mümkündür.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r4.speaker: Gazzâlî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r4.claim: Ghazali says patience is a virtue exclusive to humans: animals follow instinct without reason, while perfected angels encounter no need for patience.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r4.anchor: Gazzâlî bu erdemin, bütün yaratılmışlar içinde sadece insana verilmiş bir ayrıcalık olduğunu belirtir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r5.claim: Qur'anic examples show hardship and ease as facts of life, command the Prophet to endure like resolute messengers, and portray steadfast believers in battle; patience means trusting God's aid to overcome difficulty, not submitting passively to it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r5.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de, rahatlık ve bolluk kadar sıkıntı ve darlık da bir hayat gerçeği olarak gösterilmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r6.claim: The preceding verses call Jews, especially their religious leaders, to abandon errors, keep their pledge, recognize Muhammad's mission, believe the Qur'an and accept Islam, respect truth, pray, give zakat, and practice the good they command.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r6.anchor: Yukarıdaki âyetlerde yahudiler ve özellikle onların din önderleri, eski anlayış ve yanlışlarını terkederek Allah’a verdikleri sözü tutmaya

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r7.speaker: Fahreddin er-Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r7.claim: Razi says patience and prayer are urged because abandoning old beliefs and habits for Islam, potentially risking wealth and status, was difficult for the Jews.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r7.anchor: Fahreddin er-Râzî’ye göre yahudilerin, gerektiğinde mallarını ve itibarlarını tehlikeye atma pahasına, eski inanç ve alışkanlıklarından sıyrılarak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r8.claim: The author endorses Razi's insight and says it applies across time to any person or group in a comparable position.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r8.anchor: Kuşkusuz bu isabetli tesbit, her zaman için ve aynı konumda bulunan her kişi veya zümre hakkında da geçerlidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r9.claim: For major choices such as changing religion, rationally recognizing a faith's truth is insufficient because psychological and external pressures can sustain old mistaken beliefs and practices.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r9.anchor: insanların din değiştirmek gibi çok önemli kararlarında sadece aklî olarak bu dinin doğruluğunu kavramaları yeterli değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r10.claim: The Qur'an counsels resisting such pressures through patience as psychological and moral resolve, supported in practice and strengthened by prayer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r10.anchor: Kur’an bu güçlüğün aşılmasında belirtilen baskılara sabır denilen psikolojik ve ahlâkî irade ile direnmeyi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r11.claim: Prayer continuously sustains the relation between God and servant throughout life, strengthening faith and faith-based decisions and helping actions develop within religious and moral rules.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r11.anchor: Namaz, Allah ile kul arasındaki ilişkiyi bir ömür boyu amelî olarak sürdüren en canlı ve sürekli bir ibadet olduğu için

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r12.claim: The Qur'an explicitly says prayer restrains indecency and evil, illustrating this effect.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r12.anchor: Kuşkusuz namaz hayasızlık ve kötülükten meneder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r13.claim: Khushūʿ means heartfelt reverence and attachment to God, with submission and obedience.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r13.anchor: Terim olarak huşû “Allah’a gönülden saygı duyup bağlanmak, boyun eğip itaat etmek” demektir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r14.claim: Only those who attach themselves to God with khushūʿ receive patience's and especially prayer's positive effects.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:45/r14.anchor: Sabrın ve özellikle namazın yukarıdaki olumlu tesirinden nasibini alacak olanlar, ancak Allah’a huşû ile bağlanan

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p24/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p24/r2.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p24/r2.claim: Most scholars read the address as directed to the People of the Book while also teaching all servants; al-Wahidi says this is the stronger reading.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p24/r2.anchor: عند أكثر أهل العلم أن هذه الآية خطاب لأهل الكتاب وهو مع ذلك أدب لجميع العباد

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p24/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p24/r3.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p24/r3.claim: Some instead take the address as returning to the Muslims; al-Wahidi prefers the preceding view.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p24/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم: رجع بهذا الخطاب إلى خطاب المسلمين والقول الأول أظهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r3.claim: Sabr is restraining oneself against what is disliked; its verb is normally transitive, though the object is often omitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r3.anchor: الصبر: حبس النفس على المكروه، والفعل: صبر يصبر على فعل يفعل، وأصله أن يتعدى لواحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r4.claim: An unnamed poet depicts a free woman patiently enduring, illustrating sabr with its object understood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r4.anchor: قال الشاعر: فصبرت عارفة لذلك حرة ... ترسو إذا نفس الجبان تطلع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r5.claim: Kabīra comes from greatness or size, and kabura ʿalayya means something became difficult or burdensome; kabīr can also describe age.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r5.anchor: الكبيرة: من كبر يكبر، ويكون ذلك في الجرم وفي القدر، ويقال: كبر علي كذا، أي شق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r6.claim: A poet's lines about two children and their flock illustrate kabura for growing old.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r6.anchor: قال الشاعر: صغيرين نرعى البهم يا ليت أننا ... إلى اليوم لم نكبر ولم يكبر البهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r7.claim: Khushuʿ is close to submission and derives from softness and ease; it is also explained as submissiveness and humility.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r7.anchor: الخشوع: قريب من الخضوع، وأصله: اللين والسهولة، وقيل: الاستكانة والتذلل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r8.speaker: الليث
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r8.claim: Al-Layth distinguishes bodily khuduʿ from khushuʿ, which appears in body, sight, and voice; khashʿa is a low-lying dune.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r8.anchor: وقال الليث: الخضوع في البدن، والخشوع في البدن والبصر والصوت، والخشعة: الرملة المتطامنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r9.claim: A hadith describes the Kaaba as a low-lying mound upon water.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r9.anchor: وفي الحديث: «كانت الكعبة خشعة على الماء»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r2.claim: Istaʿīnu means seek assistance; sabr has its ordinary lexical meaning unless specified otherwise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r2.anchor: تقدم ذكر معاني استفعل عند ذكر المادة في قوله تعالى: وإياك نستعين ، وأن من تلك المعاني الطلب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r3.claim: Mujahid interprets patience as fasting, since fasting is abstention from food and Ramadan is called the month of patience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الصبر: الصوم، والصوم: صبر، لأنه إمساك عن الطعام، وسمي رمضان: شهر الصبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r4.claim: Mujahid says prayer here includes obligatory prayer and its accompanying sunnah and voluntary prayers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r4.anchor: والصلاة: هي المفروضة مع ما يتبعها من السنن والنوافل، قاله مجاهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r5.claim: Some interpret prayer as supplication with an omitted word, and construe patience as patience directed toward prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r5.anchor: وقيل: الصلاة الدعاء وقد أضمر، والصبر صلة تقيده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r6.claim: Patience is variously glossed as bearing what one's soul dislikes in obedience and work, or bearing the performance of obligatory duties, the latter reported from Ibn Abbas.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r6.anchor: فقيل: بالصبر على ما تكرهه نفوسكم من الطاعة والعمل، أو على أداء الفرائض، روي ذلك عن ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r7.claim: Other glosses make patience mean bearing sins, giving up leadership, obeying while resisting desires, waiting on one's needs from God, or enduring prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r7.anchor: أو عن المعاصي، أو على ترك الرياسة، أو على الطاعات وعن الشهوات، أو على حوائجكم إلى الله، أو على الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r8.claim: Some construe the conjunction before prayer as meaning 'upon,' taking the command as seeking help through patience upon prayer and through prayer itself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r8.anchor: توهم بعض من تكلم على القرآن، أن الواو التي في الصلاة هنا بمعنى على

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r9.claim: The command to seek help through prayer is explained by its recitation's encouragement of the afterlife and detachment from worldly life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r9.anchor: وأمروا بالاستعانة بالصلاة، لأنه يتلى فيها ما يرغب في الآخرة ويزهد في الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r10.claim: Other explanations say prayer purifies sins and softens hearts, or removes distress; the Prophet resorted to prayer when troubled.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r10.anchor: أو لما فيها من تمحيص الذنوب وترقيق القلوب، أو لما فيها من إزالة الهموم، ومنه الحديث: «كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا حز به أمر فزع إلى الصلاة»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r11.claim: When his brother Qutham's death was announced, Ibn Abbas stood to pray and recited this verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r11.anchor: وقد روي أن ابن عباس نعي إليه قثم أخوه، فقام يصلي، وتلا: واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r12.claim: Prayer is also cited as a means of seeking help because it forbids indecency and wrongdoing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r12.anchor: أو لما فيها من النهي عن الفحشاء والمنكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r13.claim: One explanation puts patience first because it removes what is undesirable, whereas prayer secures what is desirable, with negation preceding affirmation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r13.anchor: قدم الصبر على الصلاة، قيل: لأن تأثير الصبر في إزالة ما لا ينبغي، وتأثير الصلاة في حصول ما ينبغي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r14.claim: The author instead sees patience first because the prior commands impose difficult separations from ingrained habits, bribes, concealment, status, and worldly practices.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r14.anchor: ويظهر أنه قدم الاستعانة به على الاستعانة بالصلاة، لأنه سبق ذكر تكاليف عظيمة شاق فراقها على من ألفها واعتادها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r15.claim: Prayer follows because it is Islam's pillar and distinguishes Muslims from polytheists.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r15.anchor: ولما كان عمود الإسلام هو الصلاة، وبها يتميز المسلم من المشرك، أتبع الصبر بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r16.claim: Prayer recitation teaches the worshipper the revealed promises and threats, admonitions and ethics, and the creation's final destination, turning the worshipper toward the afterlife and away from the world.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r16.anchor: وبالتلاوة فيها الوقوف على ما تضمنه كتاب الله من الوعد والوعيد، والمواعظ والآداب، ومصير الخلق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r17.claim: The author concludes that the listed considerations explain the command to seek help through patience and prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r17.anchor: وهذه أمور عظيمة، فكانت البداءة بالصبر لذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r1.claim: The pronoun in 'it is surely burdensome' refers to prayer, the nearest antecedent under the grammatical default.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r1.anchor: الضمير عائد على الصلاة. هذا ظاهر الكلام، وهو القاعدة في علم العربية: أن ضمير الغائب لا يعود على غير الأقرب إلا بدليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r2.speaker: البجلي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r2.claim: Al-Bajali takes the pronoun to refer to the act of seeking help, an understood verbal noun from the command.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r2.anchor: وقيل: يعود على الاستعانة، وهو المصدر المفهوم من قوله: واستعينوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r3.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash takes it to refer to answering the Messenger, since he called them to patience and prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r3.anchor: وقيل: يعود على إجابة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، لأن الصبر والصلاة مما كان يدعو إليه، قاله الأخفش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r4.claim: Other proposed antecedents are worship implied by patience and prayer, the Kaaba toward which they were ordered to pray, or all the duties and prohibitions from remembering God's favor through seeking help.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r4.anchor: وقيل: على العبادة التي يتضمنها بالمعنى ذكر الصبر والصلاة. وقيل: يعود على الكعبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r5.claim: Another interpretation treats the pronoun as dual in sense, referring jointly to patience and prayer though expressed through one antecedent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r5.anchor: وقيل: المعنى على التثنية، واكتفى بعوده على أحدهما، فكأنه قال: وإنهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r6.speaker: مؤرج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r6.claim: Muwarraj says prayer is the more important or dominant antecedent, comparing the pronoun's return with the attraction of trade in the verse about people dispersing from Friday prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r6.anchor: قال مؤرج في عود الضمير: لأن الصلاة أهم وأغلب، كقوله تعالى: انفضوا إليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r7.claim: The author clarifies that a pronoun after conjunction with waw should agree in dual or plural number with both antecedents, unlike a pronoun following aw, which refers to only one.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r7.anchor: لأن العطف بالواو يخالف العطف بأو، فالأصل في العطف بالواو مطابقة الضمير لما قبله في تثنية وجمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p299/r8.claim: Kabara here means that prayer is heavy and difficult.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p300/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p300/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p300/r1.claim: The exception is complete: prayer is burdensome for everyone except the humble, whose humility makes its worship, hope, and promised eternal happiness easy to bear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p300/r1.anchor: استثناء مفرغ، لأن المعنى: وإنها لكبيرة على كل أحد إلا على الخاشعين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p300/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p300/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p300/r2.claim: The humble are submissive and tranquil; prayer suits their standing, bowing, prostration, and hope for God's reward, whereas hypocrites and ostentatious worshippers expect no benefit from their deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p300/r2.anchor: وهم المتواضعون المستكينون، وإنما لم تشق على الخاشعين، لأنها منطوية على أوصاف هم متحلون بها لخشوعهم

QASHANI:2:44-46/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:44-46/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:44-46/r4.claim: Seeking aid means asking the powerful for help, since people have no independent power over their actions.
QASHANI:2:44-46/r4.anchor: واطلبوا العون والمدد ممن له القدرة، إذ لا قدرة لكم على أفعالكم

QASHANI:2:44-46/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:44-46/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:44-46/r5.claim: Patience is enduring disliked things done to one and imposed on one, in order to attain contentment.
QASHANI:2:44-46/r5.anchor: على ما تكرهون مما يفعل بكم وتكلفكم ونيتكم به لكي تصلوا إلى مقام الرضا

QASHANI:2:44-46/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:44-46/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:44-46/r6.claim: Prayer is the heart’s presence to receive the manifestations of the divine attributes.

QASHANI:2:44-46/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:44-46/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:44-46/r7.claim: Prayer’s heart-presence is difficult except for humble, tender hearts that receive subtle lights and withstand overpowering manifestations, knowing themselves in their Lord’s presence, meaning the divine attributes.
QASHANI:2:44-46/r7.anchor: المنكسرة، اللينة قلوبهم لقبول أنوار التجليات اللطيفة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r1.claim: The command to seek help with patience and prayer follows the order to abandon misguidance and follow the law; those demands are hard because they require surrendering what one loves and wants, so this address treats the soul’s illness.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r1.anchor: لما أمرهم سبحانه بترك الضلال والإضلال والتزام الشرائع وكان ذلك شاقا عليهم لما فيه من فوات محبوبهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r2.claim: Ṣabr means restraining the self from what it dislikes; it precedes prayer because prayer is incomplete without patience, because it suits the addressees, or because removing harm takes precedence over gaining benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r2.anchor: حبس النفس على ما تكره وقدمه على الصلاة لأنها لا تكمل إلا به

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r3.claim: Another rationale for the order is that patience removes what is improper while prayer brings what is good, and preventing harm precedes seeking benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r3.anchor: وتأثير الصلاة في حصول ما ينبغي ودرء المفاسد مقدم على جلب المصالح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r4.claim: Ṣabr may be generic patience or specifically fasting, as suggested by its pairing with prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r4.anchor: واللام فيه للجنس ويجوز أن يراد بالصبر نوع منه وهو الصوم بقرينة ذكره مع الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r5.claim: Seeking help through patience as general endurance means awaiting relief while trusting the One who never disappoints those who rely on Him; hence the saying that patience is the key to relief.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r5.anchor: انتظار الفرج والنجحت وكلا على من لا يخيب المتوكلين عليه ولذا قيل : الصبر مفتاح الفرج

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r6.claim: If ṣabr means fasting, it breaks desire and purifies the soul, which produces devotion to God and the answer to prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r6.anchor: وبه على المعنى الثاني لما فيه من كسر الشهوة وتصفية النفس الموجبين للانقطاع إلى الله تعالى الموجب لإجابة الدعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r7.claim: Prayer provides help through its many forms of worship, which draw one near to God, bring the sought good, and ascend toward the Beloved; its five daily repetitions include intimate conversation and wash away sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r7.anchor: لما فيها من أنواع العبادة مما يقرب إلى الله تعالى قربا يقتضي الفوز بالمطلوب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r8.speaker: حذيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r8.claim: A report from Ḥudhayfa says that when a matter grieved the Prophet, he prayed.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r8.anchor: وقد روى حذيفة أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إذا حزنه أمر صلى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r9.speaker: أحمد
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r9.claim: A report transmitted by Aḥmad says the Prophet resorted to prayer whenever a matter grieved him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r9.anchor: وروى أحمد أنه إذا حزنه أمر فزع إلى الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r10.claim: Reading prayer here and in the reports as supplication is somewhat strained, and reading patience as patience specifically in prayer is even more remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r10.anchor: وحمل الصلاة على الدعاء في الآية وكذا في الحديث لا يخلو عن بعد وأبعد منه كون المراد بالصبر الصبر على الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r11.claim: The feminine pronoun in inna-hā most naturally refers to prayer; its singular reference emphasizes its greatness and prayer itself gathers several kinds of patience.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r11.anchor: الضمير للصلاة كما يقتضيه الظاهر وتخصيصها برد الضمير إليه العظم شأنها واستجماعها ضروبا من الصبر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r12.claim: Kabīrah means burdensome and difficult for those who perform prayer, as in the expression that what the Messenger calls to is burdensome for polytheists.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r12.anchor: ومعنى كبرها ثقلها وصعوبتها على من يفعلها على حد قوله تعالى : ( كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r13.claim: The exception is syntactically unrestricted: prayer is burdensome for everyone except the humble, who are lowly and submissive; the root khushūʿ denotes meekness and abasement.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r13.anchor: وهم المتواضعون المستكينون وأصلال خشوع الأخبات ومنه الخشعة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r14.claim: The word khashʿah also denotes a low, settled sand mound.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r15.claim: Prayer does not burden the humble because they know what it gives and expect its stored reward; knowledge of the goal makes its cost easy.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r15.anchor: وإنما لم تثقل عليهم لأنهم عارفون بما يحصل لهم فيها متوقعون ما ادخر من ثوابها فتهون عليهم ولذلك قيل : من عرف ما يطلب هان عليه ما يبذل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r16.claim: Another parsing makes the pronoun refer to seeking help, which is broader; the objection that seeking help cannot be burdensome fails because help through prayer is a specific performance of it for needs or other acts of obedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r16.anchor: رجوع الضمير إلى الإستعانة على حد ( إعدلوا هو أقرب للتقوى ) ورجح بالشمول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r17.claim: A further explanation treats the feminine pronoun as referring to the commands and prohibitions mentioned, whose weight is evident; this is nearer than al-Akhfash’s view that it refers to answering the Messenger, and much nearer than returning it to the Kaʿba implied by prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r17.anchor: وقيل : الضمير راجع إلى المذكورات المأمور بها والمنهي عنها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r18.claim: The author adduces the wording about God and His Messenger as a feminine pronoun referring back to a combined subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r18.anchor: يجوز أن يكون من أسلوب ( والله ورسوله أحق أن يرضوه )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r19.claim: The cited poetic example illustrates feminine agreement in a clause about the breaking of youth and hair turning gray.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r19.anchor: وقوله : إن شرخ الشباب والشعر الأس ود ما لم يعاص كان جنونا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r20.claim: A feminine pronoun may also refer to each individual item, as in the verse about those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it, according to one grammatical view.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p248/r20.anchor: والتأنيث مثله في قوله تعالى على رأي : ( والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها )

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r1.claim: Seeking help through patience and prayer is for the forms of affliction one will face.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r1.anchor: {واستعينوا} على ما يستقبلكم من أنواع البلاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r2.claim: Another view says they should seek help in pursuing the Hereafter.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r3.claim: Patience means restraining oneself from sins.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r4.claim: Another interpretation is patience in fulfilling the obligatory duties.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r4.anchor: وقيل: أراد: الصبر على أداء الفرائض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r5.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r5.claim: Mujahid identifies patience as fasting; Ramadan is called the month of patience because fasting makes one indifferent to worldly life while prayer inclines one toward the Hereafter.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الصبر الصوم، ومنه سمي شهر رمضان شهر الصبر، وذلك لأن الصوم يزهده في الدنيا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r6.claim: The conjunction may mean “with patience concerning prayer,” as in God's command to make one's family pray and patiently persevere in it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r6.anchor: وقيل: الواو بمعنى على، أي: واستعينوا بالصبر على الصلاة، كما قال الله تعالى:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r7.claim: The feminine pronoun in “it is burdensome” may refer distributively to both patience and prayer, meaning each is burdensome.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r7.anchor: {وإنها} يقل وإنهما ردا للكناية إلى كل واحد منهما أي وإن كل خصلة منهما.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r8.claim: The distributive reading is illustrated by the verse saying each of the two gardens yielded its fruit.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r9.claim: Another explanation supplies two clauses: patience is burdensome, and prayer is burdensome.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r9.anchor: وقيل: معناه {واستعينوا بالصبر} وإنه لكبير وبالصلاة وإنها لكبيرة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r10.speaker: المؤرج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r10.claim: Al-Muʿarrij refers the pronoun to prayer because prayer is more general, as the pronoun for spending in the gold-and-silver verse refers to silver.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r10.anchor: وقال المؤرج (4) رد الكناية إلى الصلاة لأنها أعم كقوله تعالى: "والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها" (34-التوبة)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r11.claim: Another view refers the pronoun to prayer because patience is included within prayer; the verse about pleasing God and His Messenger uses the singular for a similar reason.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r11.anchor: وقيل: رد الكناية إلى الصلاة لأن الصبر داخل فيها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r12.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r12.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl refers the pronoun to the act of seeking help.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r12.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل: رد الكناية إلى الاستعانة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r14.claim: The humble worshippers are the believers.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r15.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r15.claim: Al-Hasan says the humble worshippers are those who fear God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r16.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r16.claim: Another view defines the humble worshippers as the obedient.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r17.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r17.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r17.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan says they are the modest and humble.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r18.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r18.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r18.claim: The root sense of humility is stillness; as the verse says, voices are hushed to the Merciful, the humble person is settled in obedience to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p89/r18.anchor: وأصل الخشوع السكون قال الله تعالى: "وخشعت الأصوات للرحمن" (108-طه) فالخاشع ساكن إلى طاعة الله تعالى.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r1.claim: This command follows the preceding one: patience and prayer ease difficult duties involving effort, relinquishing leadership, and turning away from wealth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r1.anchor: متصل بما قبله، كأنهم لما أمروا بما يشق عليهم لما فيه من الكلفة وترك الرياسة والإعراض عن المال عولجوا بذلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r2.claim: Patience can mean waiting hopefully for success and relief while relying on God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r2.anchor: استعينوا على حوائجكم بانتظار النجح والفرج توكلا على الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r3.claim: Alternatively, patience means fasting: refraining from invalidators breaks desire and purifies the soul.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r3.anchor: أو بالصوم الذي هو صبر عن المفطرات لما فيه من كسر الشهوة، وتصفية النفس.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r4.claim: Prayer gathers bodily and inward worship, including purification, covering, spending, facing the Kaaba, worship, humility, sincere intention, resisting Satan, intimate supplication, recitation, testimony, and restraint from food and drink.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r4.anchor: فإنها جامعة لأنواع العبادات النفسانية والبدنية، من الطهارة وستر العورة وصرف المال فيهما، والتوجه إلى الكعبة والعكوف للعبادة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r5.claim: Prayer helps attain aims and repair afflictions.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r5.anchor: حتى تجابوا إلى تحصيل المآرب وجبر المصائب

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r6.speaker: النبي
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r6.claim: A report says that whenever a matter distressed the Prophet, he turned to prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r6.anchor: روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان إذا حزبه أمر فزع إلى الصلاة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45/r7.claim: The word prayer may instead mean supplication.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45#2/r1.claim: The feminine pronoun may refer to seeking help through both means, or to prayer alone because of its importance and its many forms of patience, or to all the commands and prohibitions.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45#2/r1.anchor: أي وإن الاستعانة بهما أو الصلاة وتخصيصها برد الضمير إليها، لعظم شأنها واستجماعها ضروبا من الصبر. أو جملة ما أمروا بها ونهوا عنها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45#2/r2.claim: Kabīra means heavy and difficult, as in al-Shūrā 42:13.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45#2/r3.claim: The humble are those who submit inwardly; khushūʿ is humility, like a low sand mound.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45#2/r3.anchor: { إلا على الخشعين } أي المخبتين، والخشوع الإخبات ومنه الخشعة للرملة المتطامنة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45#2/r4.claim: Khushūʿ is bodily humility, while khuḍūʿ is softness and compliance and is attributed to the heart.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:45#2/r4.anchor: والخضوع اللين والانقياد، ولذلك يقال الخشوع بالجوارح والخضوع بالقلب.

SULAMI:v1p58#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r1.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r1.claim: Sahl says patience and prayer are aids to establishing religion and steadfast certainty.
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r1.anchor: قال سهل بن عبد الله : استعينوا بها على إقامة الدين وثبات اليقين .

SULAMI:v1p58#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r2.claim: Ibn Ata says patience and prayer help one reach the depths of spiritual realities.
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : استعينوا بهما على البلوغ إلى درك الحقائق

SULAMI:v1p58#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r3.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r3.claim: Abu Uthman says patience and prayer help make one's time free for devotion.
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r3.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان : استعينوا بهما على فراغة أوقاتكم .

SULAMI:v1p58#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r4.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r4.claim: Prayer is daunting for the person whose heart, spirit, and secret bow to the arrivals of awe and flashes of majesty.
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r4.anchor: ﴿ وإنها لكبيرة ﴾ الآية . قال : لمن خشع قلبه وروحه وسره لموارد الهيبة وطوالع الإجلال .

SULAMI:v1p58#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r5.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r5.claim: Abu Uthman says it is daunting only to one whose limbs humbly perform worship, rejoicing in the majesty of the Commander's address.
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r5.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : ﴿ وإنها لكبيرة إلا على الخاشعين ﴾ قال : لمن ذلت جوارحه للعبادات فرحا بمجل خطاب الآمر فيه .

SULAMI:v1p58#3/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r6.speaker: بعض العراقيين
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r6.claim: Some Iraqis define patience as patience away from all besides God and prayer as standing before God with proper courtesy; only the eternally elect find this easy.
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r6.anchor: وقال بعض العراقيين : استعينوا بالصبر عمن دون الله والصلاة الوقوف بحسن الأدب مع الله ، وإنها لكبيرة إلا على الخاشعين إلا على من أيد في الأزل بخصائص الاجتباء .

SULAMI:v1p58#3/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r7.claim: One view says believers can attain patience and prayer only through God's help.
SULAMI:v1p58#3/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم : استعينوا بي في الصبر والصلاة فإنهما لا يحصلان لكم إلا بمعونتي .

BIQAI-FULL:v1p120/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p120/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p120/r5.claim: When Umar grieved at the Prophet's condition, the Prophet asked whether he was content that others have this world while they have the hereafter.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p120/r5.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لعمر رضي الله عنه لما رثى لحاله : ( أما ترضى أن تكون لهم الدنيا ولنا الآخرة ؟ )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p120/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p120/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p120/r6.claim: Patience restrains the soul even from lawful desires; this is its purification, while exhausting it through restraint gives it life and indulging it corrupts it, as the sun chapter says.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p120/r6.anchor: وصبر النفس عن شهواتها وإن كانت حلالا هو حقيقة تزكيتها , وقتلها بإضنائها منها هو حياتها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r9.claim: Their attachment to leadership made them resist becoming followers of Arabs after seeing themselves as masters of the earth, so patience is prescribed to compel them to accept following truth.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r9.anchor: ما تعودت به أنفسهم من الرياسة والتقدم فلما في ذلك عليهم من المشقة أن يصيروا أتباعا للعرب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r10.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r10.claim: Patience helps them demonstrate truth and submit to it by restraining the soul from habit and desire and purifying it; this light lets the heart see beyond the panic of leaving familiar ways and includes fasting and other patience.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r10.anchor: والصبر حبس النفس عن حاجتها وعادتها وعلى إصلاحها وتزكيتها , هو ضياء للقلوب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r11.claim: Prayer connects the worshipper to the highest station.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p125/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125/r1.claim: True prayer restrains its practitioner from falsehood and commands holding to truth and returning to it; prayer with this quality, supported by patience against desire, leads to salvation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125/r1.anchor: من لم تنهه صلاته عن ركوب الباطل والتمادي فيه وتأمره بلزوم الحق والرجوع إليه فليس بمصل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p125/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125/r2.claim: Prayer is mentioned second because it is provision from God, sparing them from buying silence or concealment from their followers; the command to persist in family prayer promises that God provides.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125/r2.anchor: وثنى بالصلاة لأنها استرزاق يغنيهم عن اشتراء ثمن كانوا يأخذونه من أتباعهم في اللبس والكتمان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r1.claim: Al-Harali allows ṣabr to mean supplication: patience from base desires and hardship, completed by fasting, prayer, and turning to God, enlightens the heart and reaches the highest righteousness.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r1.anchor: قال الحرالي . ويصح أن يراد بها الدعاء , فمن صبر عن الدنايا وعلى المكاره

BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r2.claim: He glosses prayer as weighty because al-kabīr denotes greatness of rank or magnitude, whether perceptible outwardly or inwardly.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r2.anchor: والكبير ما جل قدره أو مقداره في حس ظاهر أو في معنى باطن - قاله الحرالي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r3.claim: Prayer is easy only for the humble, receptive servants who have no pride and consider the outcome and reward; others perform it unwillingly or avoid it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r3.anchor: إلا على الخاشعين } أي المخبتين الذين هم في غاية السهولة واللين والتواضع لربهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r4.claim: The Prophet describes prayer as the delight of his eyes.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r4.anchor: ولذا قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( وجعلت قرة عيني في الصلاة )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r5.claim: Al-Harali defines khushūʿ as the stillness of limbs and thoughts around what matters most in the present moment.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r5.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهو أي الخشوع هدو الجوارح والخواطر فيما هو الأهم في الوقت

BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r6.claim: Prayer's greatness means only a humble person who leaves self-interest and accepts the abasement of servitude can truly undertake it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r6.anchor: وأنبأ تعالى بكبر قدر الصلاة عن أن يتناول عملها إلا خاشع خرج عن حظ نفسه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r7.claim: The verse alludes to the afternoon prayer and the final Prophet's era and condition of servitude; this is difficult for those who associate prophethood with kingship unless they humble themselves.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r7.anchor: وفي إشارة كمال الصلاة إشعار بصلاة العصر التي هي صلاة النبي الخاتم الذي زمنه وقت العصر وحالة العبودية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r8.claim: Prayer is singled out as great because patience diminishes the self, whereas prayer turns toward the Real, God the Most High and Great.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r8.anchor: وخصت الصلاة بالكبر دون الصبر لأن الصب صغار للنفس والصلاة وجهة للحق والله هو العلي الكبير - انتهى .

BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r16.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r16.claim: Al-Harali says prayer as unseen communion becomes possible through expecting acceptance after death; this is the state of one whose deeds and life favor the Hereafter, while ẓann accommodates people below certainty.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p125#2/r16.anchor: قال الحرالي : ولما كان في الصلاة مناجاة لله على الغيب كانت إنما تتيسر على من يظن القبول

TUSTARI:2:45/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:45/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:45/r1.claim: Patience here means fasting, while prayer is a connection to gnosis.
TUSTARI:2:45/r1.anchor: الصبر ها هنا الصوم والصلاة وصلة المعرفة

TUSTARI:2:45/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:45/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:45/r2.claim: Prayer that truly connects leaves no complaint against God: asking itself is an accusation, and connection removes the need to ask.
TUSTARI:2:45/r2.anchor: فمن صحت له الصلاة، وهي الوصلة، لم يبق له على الله تهمة، إذ السؤال تهمة، ولا يبقى السؤال مع الوصلة

DURR-FULL:v1p158/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r5.claim: Patience and prayer are two helps from God, so believers should seek help through them.
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة} قال: إنهما معونتان من الله فاستعينوا بهما

DURR-FULL:v1p158/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r6.claim: Patience means acknowledging to God what He has sent and expecting reward from Him; someone may be inwardly despairing while outwardly appearing patient.
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: الصبر اعتراف العبد لله بما أصاب منه واحتسابه عند الله رجاء ثوابه وقد يجزع الرجل وهو متجلد

DURR-FULL:v1p158/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r7.claim: Umar distinguishes patience through affliction from the still better patience of refraining from God's prohibitions.
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r7.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: الصبر صبران: صبر عند المصيبة حسن وأحسن منه الصبر عن محارم الله

DURR-FULL:v1p158/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd defines patience as enduring what God loves despite its bodily or emotional burden and resisting what God dislikes despite one's desires.
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r8.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال: الصبر بابين الصبر لله فيما أحب وإن ثقل على الأنفس والأبدان والصبر عما كره وإن نازعت إليه الاهواء

DURR-FULL:v1p163/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r1.speaker: غير مسمى
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r1.claim: The report says God enriches those who seek sufficiency, grants patience to those who seek it, and gives no gift better or more abundant than patience.
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r1.anchor: يغنه الله ومن يتصبر يصبره الله ولم تعطوا عطاءا خيرا وأوسع من الصبر

DURR-FULL:v1p163/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r2.claim: Umar says patience was the best life they found.
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r2.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: وجدنا خير عيشنا الصبر

DURR-FULL:v1p163/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r3.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r3.claim: Maymun b. Mihran says a person obtains no great good except through patience.
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r3.anchor: عن ميمون بن مهران قال: ما نال رجلا من جسيم الخير شيء إلا بالصبر

DURR-FULL:v1p163/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliya says prayer is a means of seeking God's good pleasure, and both patience and prayer are acts of obedience to Him.
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r4.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله {واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة} قال: على مرضاة الله واعلموا أنهما من طاعة الله

DURR-FULL:v1p163/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r5.speaker: حذيفة
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r5.claim: Hudhayfa reports that whenever something distressed the Prophet, he resorted to prayer.
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r5.anchor: عن حذيفة قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا حز به أمر فزع إلى الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v1p163/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r6.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r6.claim: Abu al-Darda says that on windy nights the Prophet sought refuge in the mosque until the wind ceased and turned to prayer during solar or lunar eclipses.
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r6.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا كانت ليلة ريح كان مفزعه إلى المسجد حتى يسكن

DURR-FULL:v1p163/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r7.speaker: صهيب
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r7.claim: The Prophet's practice, and that of earlier prophets, was to resort to prayer when frightened.
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r7.anchor: عن صهيب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال كانوا - يعني الأنبياء - يفزعون إذا فزعوا إلى الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v1p163/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r8.claim: When told that his son had died during a journey, Ibn Abbas dismounted, prayed two units, and said they had acted as God commanded.
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه كان في مسير له فنعي إليه ابن له فنزل فصلى ركعتين ثم استرجع وقال: فعلنا كما أمرنا الله

DURR-FULL:v1p163/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r9.claim: When told of his brother Qutham's death, Ibn Abbas recited the return formula, left the road, prayed two units with a long sitting, and repeated the verse before resuming his journey.
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه نعي إليه أخوه قثم وهو في مسير فاسترجع ثم تنحى عن الطريق فصلى ركعتين أطال فيهما الجلوس

DURR-FULL:v1p163/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r10.speaker: عبادة بن محمد بن عبادة بن الصامت
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r10.claim: At Ubadah's death, he forbade mourning, directed his companions to perform ablution, pray in the mosque, and seek forgiveness for him and themselves, then asked them to hurry him to the grave.
DURR-FULL:v1p163/r10.anchor: عن عبادة بن محمد بن عبادة بن الصامت قال: لما حضرت عبادة الوفاة قال: أحرج على إنسان منكم يبكي

DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r1.speaker: أم كلثوم بنت عقبة
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r1.claim: When her husband Abdurrahman fainted and seemed near death, Umm Kulthum went to the mosque to seek help through patience and prayer; he later recounted two angels' summons and another angel's assurance of his prenatal blessed fate, and lived a month longer.
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r1.anchor: أم كلثوم بنت عقبة وكانت من المهاجرات الأول في قوله {واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة} قالت: غشي على الرحمن بن عبد الرحمن غشية

DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل بن حبان
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r2.claim: Seek the afterlife through patient fulfillment of obligations and preserve prayer's times, recitation, bowing, prostration, takbir, tashahhud, blessings on the Prophet, and full upright form; this constitutes completing prayer.
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r2.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حبان في قوله {واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة} يقول: استعينوا على طلب الآخرة بالصبر على الفرائض والصلاة فحافظوا عليها وعلى مواقيتها

DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل بن حبان
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r3.claim: He says the prayer's burden was the change from Jerusalem toward the Kaaba, which weighed on hypocrites and Jews; the humble are the meek.
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r3.anchor: قوله {وإنها لكبيرة إلا على الخاشعين} يقول: صرفك عن بيت المقدس إلى الكعبة كبر ذلك على المنافقين واليهود

DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the prayer as weighty.
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله {وإنها لكبيرة} قال: لثقيلة

DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the polytheists told Muhammad that the prayer and faith in God were a great thing he was summoning them to.
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله {وإنها لكبيرة} قال: قال المشركون واله يا محمد إنك لتدعونا إلى أمر كبير

DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the humble as those who believe what God revealed.
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {إلا على الخاشعين} قال: المصدقين بما أنزل الله

DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r7.claim: Mujahid says the humble are true believers.
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {إلا على الخاشعين} قال: المؤمنين حقا

DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r8.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r8.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the humble are those who fear God.
DURR-FULL:v1p163#2/r8.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله {إلا على الخاشعين} قال: الخائفين

AKHFASH:v1p87/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p87/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p87/r1.claim: The feminine pronoun in “it is burdensome” refers specifically to prayer; the clause is construed with the nearer noun الصلاة.
AKHFASH:v1p87/r1.anchor: أما قوله {واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة وإنها لكبيرة} فلأنه حمل الكلام على "الصلاة".

AKHFASH:v1p87/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p87/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p87/r2.claim: With coordination by wāw, the predicate most naturally applies to both coordinated nouns, as in “Zayd and ʿAmr are going.”
AKHFASH:v1p87/r2.anchor: وأقيس هذا اذا ما كان بالواو ان يحمل عليهما جميعا. تقول: "زيد وعمرو ذاهبان".

AKHFASH:v1p87/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p87/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p87/r3.claim: With aw, the predicate describes only one of the two; it may follow either, but the latter is more apt because it is nearer to the predicate.
AKHFASH:v1p87/r3.anchor: بالخيار ان شئت جعلت الكلام على الأول وان شئت على الآخر، وأن تحمله على الآخر أقيس

AKHFASH:v1p87/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p87/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p87/r4.claim: An anonymous line using “aw ḥusn al-nisāʾ” is cited as evidence for how a predicate can follow one coordinated alternative.
AKHFASH:v1p87/r4.anchor: قال الشاعر: [من البسيط وهو الشاهد الثامن والخمسون] : أما الوسامة أو حسن النساء فقد * أوتيت منه لو ان العقل محتنك

AKHFASH:v1p87/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p87/r5.speaker: ابن أحمر
AKHFASH:v1p87/r5.claim: Ibn Aḥmar's line is cited as a poetic example of the coordination construction under discussion.
AKHFASH:v1p87/r5.anchor: وقال ابن أحمر: [من الطويل وهو الشاهد التاسع والخمسون] : [38ء] رماني بداء كنت منه ووالدي * بريئا

AKHFASH:v1p87/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p87/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p87/r6.claim: An anonymous line contrasts “what we have” with “what you have” and is offered as another example of the construction.
AKHFASH:v1p87/r6.anchor: وقال الآخر: [من المنسرح وهو الشاهد الستون] : نحن بما عندنا وأنت بما * عندك راض والرأي مختلف

AKHFASH:v1p87/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p87/r7.speaker: البرجمي
AKHFASH:v1p87/r7.claim: Al-Burjumī's line about being a stranger with Qiyār at Medina is cited as a parallel coordination example.
AKHFASH:v1p87/r7.anchor: وهذا مثل قول البرجمي: [من الطويل وهو الشاهد الحادي والستون] : من يك أمسى بالمدينة داره * فإني وقيارا بها لغريب

IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet says fasting is half of patience.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r1.anchor: عن رجل من بني سليم عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال : الصوم نصف الصبر .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : واستعينوا بالصبر قال الصبر الصيام .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r7.claim: Seek God's pleasure through patience and prayer, recognizing that both are obedience to God.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r7.anchor: عن أبي العالية يقول : استعينوا بالصبر والصلاة على مرضاة الله ، واعلموا انها من طاعة الله .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r8.speaker: محمد بن طلحة الأسدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r8.claim: Muhammad ibn Talha al-Asadi says patience means fasting.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r8.anchor: عن محمد بن طلحة الاسدي يقول : استعينوا بالصبر على الصيام .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r9.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r9.claim: Muqatil says to seek the afterlife through patience in fulfilling obligations and through prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r9.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان قوله : واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة قال : استعينوا على طلب الاخرة بالصبر على الفرائض والصلاة .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r10.speaker: بعضهم
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r10.claim: Some interlocutors said patience means prayer, citing this verse as evidence.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r10.anchor: فقال بعضهم : هو الصلاة ونزعوا بقول الله : واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r11.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r11.speaker: أبو بكر حبش بن الورد البغدادي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r11.claim: Abu Bakr rejects equating patience with prayer because God names patience and prayer as two separate things.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r11.anchor: فقال : قد ميز الله بينهما ، فقال : استعينوا بالصبر والصلاة فلم يجعله صلاة ، وقال : جعلهما شيئين

IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r12.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r12.speaker: بعضهم
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r12.claim: Some interlocutors identified patience as fasting.

IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r13.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r13.speaker: بعضهم
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r13.claim: Some interlocutors defined patience as enduring a thing, but Abu Bakr was unsatisfied with their answer.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r13.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الصبر ان يصبر على الشئ . فقال : ما معنى يصبر ؟ فلم يرض جواب أحد .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r14.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r14.speaker: أبو بكر حبش بن الورد البغدادي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r14.claim: When asked for his own definition, Abu Bakr says patience is steadfastness in a matter.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r14.anchor: وسالوه ان يخبرهم ، فقال : الصبر هو الثبات في الشئ .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r1.claim: Umar distinguishes two kinds of patience: good patience during calamity and better patience in avoiding God's prohibitions.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r1.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب قال : الصبر صبران ، صبر عند المصيبة حسن ، واحسن منه الصبر عن محارم الله .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r2.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r2.claim: The author says al-Hasan gave an account similar to Umar's distinction.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r2.anchor: قال أبو محمد : وروى عن الحسن نحو قول عمر .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r3.claim: Patience is acknowledging to God what has afflicted one, entrusting it to Him, and hoping for reward; a person may appear composed while inwardly anguished.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r3.anchor: ان سيعد بن جبير قال : الصبر اعتراف العبد لله بما اصاب فيه ، واحتسابه عند الله ، ورجاء ثوابه ، وقد يجزع الرجل وهو يتجلد لا يرى منه الا الصبر .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r4.claim: Mujahid says “it is indeed heavy” refers to prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله وانها لكبيرة قال : الصلاة .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r5.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله : وانها لكبيرة قال لثقيلة .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r6.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r6.claim: Muqatil says the difficult matter is the change from Jerusalem to the Kaaba, which burdened hypocrites and Jews.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r6.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان في قوله : وانها لكبيرة يقول صرفك من بيت المقدس إلى الكعبة ، كبير ذلك على المنافقين واليهود .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the humble as those who affirm what God revealed.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس : الا على الخاشعين يقول : المصدقين بما انزل الله تعالى .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r8.claim: Mujahid identifies the humble as true believers.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : وانها لكبيرة الا على الخاشعين قال المؤمنين حقا .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r9.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r9.claim: Al-Aliyah says the humble are those who fear God.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r9.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله : الا على الخاشعين قال يعني الخائفين .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r10.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r10.claim: Muqatil glosses the humble as the meek or humble.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p102/r10.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان قوله : الا على الخاشعين يعني به المتواضعين .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r1.claim: The address remains to the Israelites and teaches what will enable them to fulfill the commands and prohibitions just listed; after exhortation and warning, patience and prayer are the remedy for the drag of old habits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r1.anchor: خطاب لبني إسرائيل بالإرشاد إلى ما يعينهم على التخلق بجميع ما عدد لهم من الأوامر والنواهي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r2.claim: Patience helps because attachment to familiar ways and weakness in leaving them impede peoples from following a sound religion; patience makes accepting truth easier.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r2.anchor: فإذا تدرعوا بالصبر سهل عليهم اتباع الحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r3.claim: Prayer here renews and strengthens the earlier command to establish prayer in 2:43, using confidence in the addressees as a subtle form of encouragement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r3.anchor: فالمراد تأكد الأمر بها الذي في قوله : { وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r4.claim: He rejects the view that ‘seek help’ shifts to Muslims: the conjunction signals continuity, and the following description of the humble as believers confirms the Israelite address.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r4.anchor: وهذا وهم لأن وجود حرف العطف ينادي على خلاف ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r5.claim: The author says it is no objection that unbelievers are being asked to use prayer: 2:43 likewise commands prayer and alms while addressing the Israelites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r5.anchor: وقريب منه آنفا قوله تعالى : { وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة واركعوا مع الراكعين }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r6.speaker: الغزالي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r6.claim: Al-Ghazali defines religious patience as the steadfastness of the religious motive against the motive of appetite; the author finds this apt to the verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r6.anchor: ثبات باعث الدين في مقابلة باعث الشهوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r7.claim: More generally, patience is enduring and remaining steady through what displeases the self, whether for later good or reward, or because escape is impossible, while avoiding panic and vexation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r7.anchor: فالصبر احتمال وثبات على ما لا يلائم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r8.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r8.claim: A report in the Ṣaḥīḥ says that true, complete patience occurs at the first shock; the author explains this as patience before one knows escape is impossible, while later calm acceptance is still real patience.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477#2/r8.anchor: ورد في ( الصحيح ) : ( إنما الصبر عند الصدمة الأولى )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r1.claim: Prayer here means the Islamic ritual as a comprehensive act of praising God in speech, deed, and belief; thus the two means of help are patience and gratitude.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r1.anchor: وهي مجموع محامد لله تعالى ، قولا وعملا واعتقادا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r2.speaker: الغزالي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r2.claim: Al-Ghazali says faith is half patience and half gratitude; the author calls this a good observation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r2.anchor: وقد قيل إن الإيمان نصفه صبر ونصفه شكر كما في ( الإحياء )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r3.claim: Patience underlies the virtues because moral excellence depends on strong will and restraining appetite and anger; for example, forbearance, generosity, learning, piety, courage, justice, and work all involve patience.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r3.anchor: فما التحلم والتكرم والتعلم والتقوى والشجاعة والعدل والعمل في الأرض ونحوها إلا من ضروب الصبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r4.speaker: علي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r4.claim: A saying attributed to Ali captures the point that courage is patience for an hour.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r4.anchor: ومما يؤثر عن علي رضي الله عنه : الشجاعة صبر ساعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r5.speaker: زفر بن الحارث الكلابي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r5.claim: Zufar ibn al-Harith al-Kilabi excuses his people's retreat by saying their opponents proved more patient in facing death.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r6.claim: Qur'an 103:1–3 makes patience complete the means of success; the Qur'an also links patience with leadership, Israel's favor, and divine companionship, as the author notes through al-Ghazali.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r6.anchor: وحسبك بمزية الصبر أن الله جعله مكمل سبب الفوز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r7.speaker: الغزالي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r7.claim: Al-Ghazali says the Qur'an mentions patience in more than seventy places, associates most good and ranks with it, and makes it their fruit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r7.anchor: ذكر الله الصبر في القرآن في نيف وسبعين موضعا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r8.claim: Faith itself entails patience: accepting what lies beyond sense, obeying a human messenger, and departing from inherited religions oppose the self's habits; patience makes these duties easier for truth's sake.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p478/r8.anchor: فإن فيه مخالفة النفس هواها ومألوفها في التصديق بما هو مغيب عن الحس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p479#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p479#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p479#2/r1.claim: Commentators differ over ‘it is difficult’: some take the pronoun as prayer, which burdens the self; another takes it as seeking help through patience and prayer, by analogy with 5:8; al-Zamakhshari allows it to refer to all commands from 2:40 through 2:45.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p479#2/r1.anchor: اختلف المفسرون في معاد ضمير { إنها } فقيل عائد إلى الصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p479#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p479#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p479#2/r2.claim: The author prefers the broadest antecedent, all the preceding commands, as the clearest and most inclusive reading; he considers all these referents intended.
