IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p479#2/r2.anchor: وهذا أوضح الأقوال وأجمعها والمحامل مرادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p479#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p479#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p479#2/r3.claim: ‘Great’ means difficult or burdensome here, a familiar metaphor because hardship accompanies carrying or achieving something great; Qur'anic parallels use the same sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p479#2/r3.anchor: والمراد بالكبيرة هنا الصعبة التي تشق على النفوس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r1.claim: Khushūʿ literally denotes shrinking or lowering; al-Nābigha's ‘a low, worn water-trough rim’ illustrates the loss of height, while submission is another form of lowering.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r2.speaker: جعفر بن عبلة الحارثي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r2.claim: Jaʿfar ibn ʿAblah's verse uses ‘I humbled myself’ in the sense of submitting; the author explains inward humility as stillness and restraint from refusal or disobedience.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r3.claim: The humble here discipline and tame the self, train it to rest in God's command and seek good outcomes, and avoid being deceived by immediate desire; such a soul is ready to receive good.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r3.anchor: والمراد بالخاشع هنا الذي ذلل نفسه وكسر سورتها وعودها أن تطمئن إلى أمر الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r4.claim: The humble may be understood as those who fear and consider future consequences; patience's restraint and prayer's fixed times then become easier despite competing desires, work, or pleasure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r4.anchor: وكأن المراد بالخاشعين هنا الخائفون الناظرون في العواقب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r5.speaker: كثير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r5.claim: Kathīr's verse illustrates that when the self is prepared for an affliction, it becomes submissive to it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r5.anchor: إذا وطنت يوما لها النفس ذلت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r6.claim: Many laws aim to train this disposition, with fasting the greatest example.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r6.anchor: وأحسب أن مشروعية أحكام كثيرة قصد الشارع منها هذا المعنى وأعظمها الصوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r7.claim: He rejects restricting humility to the inward reverence of standing in prayer described by Ibn Rushd: that is a feature of prayer and the worshipper's excellence, so it cannot explain why prayer is easier for the one told to seek help through prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r7.anchor: ولا يصح حمل الخشوع هنا على خصوص الخشوع في الصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r8.claim: The clause about expecting to meet God explains the humble and shows the source of their humility; ‘expect’ means firm conviction here, since Arabic often uses ẓann for certainty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p480/r8.anchor: فدل على أن المراد من الظن هنا الإعتقاد الجازم وإطلاق الظن في كلام العرب على معنى اليقين كثير جدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r1.speaker: أوس بن حجر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r1.claim: Aws ibn Ḥajar's ‘certain in his expectation’ shows ẓann can mean certainty, not merely probability.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r2.speaker: دريد بن الصمة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r2.claim: Durayd ibn al-Ṣimmah likewise uses ẓann for a confident belief about two thousand armored men; the word can signify either certain or probable belief.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r3.claim: Meeting God and returning to Him are metaphors for resurrection and judgment, or for vision and reward, since bodily meeting and return to a place one left are impossible here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r3.anchor: والملاقاة والرجوع هنا مجازان عن الحساب والحشر أو عن الرؤية والثواب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r4.claim: The passage indirectly praises Muslims and urges the Israelites to emulate believers; if the address instead shifts to Muslims, it indirectly censures Jews and hypocrites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r4.anchor: والمقصود من قوله : { وإنها لكبيرة } إلخ التعريض بالثناء على المسلمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r5.claim: Mulaqāt derives from laqiya, meeting as presence; here it means appearing before God for judgment and thus believing in resurrection, as in the earlier Adam passage and later references.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p481/r5.anchor: واللقاء الحضور كما تقدم في قوله : { فتلقى آدم من ربه كلمات }

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r9.speaker: مقاتل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r9.claim: Muqatil interprets seeking help through patience and prayer as help in pursuing the afterlife.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r10.speaker: غيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r10.claim: Another interpretation makes patience abstention from disobedience and desires for God's pleasure, and prayer a means to pleasure and forgiveness and help in worldly calamities.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r10.anchor: استعينوا بالصبر عن الطاعات وعن الشهوات على نيل رضوان الله، وبالصلاة على نيل الرضوان وحط الذنوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r11.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r11.claim: A report says the Prophet resorted to prayer whenever a matter distressed him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r11.anchor: ومنه الحديث: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا كربه أمر فزع إلى الصلاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r12.claim: When told during travel that his brother Qutham had died, Ibn Abbas prayed before returning to his mount, reciting this verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r12.anchor: أن عبد الله بن عباس نعي إليه أخوه قثم، وهو في سفر، فاسترجع وتنحى عن الطريق وصلى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r13.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r13.claim: Mujahid identifies patience here as fasting, hence Ramadan's designation as the month of patience.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r13.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الصبر في هذه الآية الصوم، ومنه قيل لرمضان شهر الصبر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r14.claim: On Mujahid's reading, fasting and prayer are paired because fasting curbs desire and attachment to this world, while prayer restrains indecency, humbles, and recalls the afterlife through Quran recitation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r14.anchor: في أن الصيام يمنع الشهوات ويزهد في الدنيا، والصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر وتخشع.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r15.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r15.claim: Some take patience in its ordinary sense and prayer to mean supplication, paralleling steadfastness and remembrance in 8:45.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r15.anchor: وقال قوم: «الصبر» على بابه، والصلاة الدعاء، وتجيء هذه الآية على هذا القول مشبهة لقوله تعالى:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r16.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r16.claim: One view takes the feminine pronoun in وإنها as referring to prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r16.anchor: فقيل على الصلاة، وقيل على الاستعانة التي يقتضيها قوله واستعينوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r17.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r17.claim: Another view takes the pronoun as the act of seeking help implied by the command to seek help.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r17.anchor: على الاستعانة التي يقتضيها قوله واستعينوا، وقيل على العبادة التي يتضمنها بالمعنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r18.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r18.claim: A third view takes the pronoun as worship implied by the mention of patience and prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r18.anchor: على العبادة التي يتضمنها بالمعنى ذكر الصبر والصلاة.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p137/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p137/r1.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p137/r1.claim: One reported view says the pronoun refers to responding to Muhammad; Ibn Atiyya rejects it as weak because the verse provides no evidence for it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p137/r1.anchor: وقالت فرقة: على إجابة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم. قال القاضي أبو محمد رحمه الله: وفي هذا ضعف، لأنه لا دليل له من الآية عليه.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p137/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p137/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p137/r2.claim: Another view takes the pronoun to mean the Kaaba, since prayer is directed toward it; Ibn Atiyya calls this weaker still.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p137/r2.anchor: وقيل: يعود الضمير على الكعبة، لأن الأمر بالصلاة إنما هو إليها. قال القاضي أبو محمد رحمه الله: وهذا أضعف من الذي قبله.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p137/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p137/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p137/r3.claim: كبيرة means weighty and difficult; the humble are submissive and subdued, with an inward state shown in bodily stillness and humility.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p137/r3.anchor: و «كبيرة» معناه ثقيلة شاقة، والخاشعون المتواضعون المخبتون، والخشوع هيئة في النفس

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#3/r1.claim: Mujahid interprets patience here as fasting.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#3/r1.anchor: أي: بالصوم. في قول مجاهد (2) رحمه الله.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#3/r2.claim: Fasting and Ramadan are called patience because the faster restrains himself from food and drink.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#3/r2.anchor: ويقال لشهر رمضان: شهر الصبر (3) ، وللصائم صابر.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#3/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#3/r3.claim: A restrained animal used as a target is called maṣbūra; patience shares the sense of holding something back.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#3/r3.anchor: وكل من حبس شيئا فقد صبره. ومنه المصبورة التي نهي عنها،

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#3/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#3/r4.claim: One is called patient in adversity because he restrains himself from despair.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r1.claim: The root sense of patience is restraint: the patient restrains himself from grief.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r1.anchor: الأصل في الصبر الحبس فالصابر حابس لنفسه عن الجزع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r2.claim: Fasting is called patience because the faster restrains himself from food, drink, and sexual intercourse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r2.anchor: وسمي الصائم صابرا لحبسه نفسه عن الأكل والشرب والجماع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r3.claim: A restrained animal used as a target is called maṣbūra.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r4.claim: Mujahid says patience here means fasting.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r5.claim: One view says they were commanded to be patient in performing the religious obligations.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r5.anchor: أداء الفرائض قاله ابن عباس و مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r6.claim: A second view says the command is patience in leaving sins.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r7.claim: A third view reads the command as forgoing leadership or status and addresses the two scriptural communities.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r7.anchor: عدم الرئاسة وهو خطاب لأهل الكتابين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r8.claim: Prayer helps because its recitation encourages desire for the afterlife and detachment from worldly life.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r8.anchor: أنه يتلى فيها ما يرغب في الآخرة ويزهد في الدنيا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، مجاهد، الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r9.claim: The pronoun in wa-innahā refers to prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r9.anchor: أحدها أنه الصلاة قاله ابن عباس والحسن و مجاهد والجمهور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r10.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس، مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r10.claim: A second view takes the pronoun to refer to the Kaaba and the qibla, implied by mention of prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r10.anchor: أنها الكعبة والقبلة لأنه لما ذكر الصلاة دلت على القبلة ذكره الضحاك عن ابن عباس وبه قال مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r11.speaker: محمد بن القاسم النحوي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r11.claim: A third grammatical view takes the pronoun to refer to seeking help, which the preceding command names.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75#2/r11.anchor: انها الاستعانة لأنه لما قال واستعينوا دل على الاستعانة ذكره محمد ابن القاسم النحوي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p76/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p76/r1.speaker: الحسن، الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p76/r1.claim: They explain kabīra as heavy or burdensome, as in the verse saying what Muhammad calls to is burdensome for polytheists.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p76/r1.anchor: الكبيرة الثقيلة مثل قوله تعالى ﴿ كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه ﴾ الشورى 13

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p76/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p76/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p76/r2.claim: Khushūʿ literally involves lowering oneself and humility; it is also explained as stillness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p76/r2.anchor: والخشوع في اللغة التطامن والتواضع وقيل السكون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r1.claim: God commands people to seek help through patience and prayer in pursuing the good of this life and the next.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r1.anchor: آمرا عبيده، فيما يؤملون من خير الدنيا والآخرة، بالاستعانة بالصبر والصلاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r2.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan says patience in this verse means enduring the obligations while seeking the afterlife, alongside prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r2.anchor: كما قال مقاتل بن حيان في تفسير هذه الآية: استعينوا على طلب الآخرة بالصبر على الفرائض، والصلاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies patience here as fasting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r3.anchor: فأما الصبر فقيل: إنه الصيام، نص عليه مجاهد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r4.claim: A report from a man of Banu Sulaym says the Prophet called fasting half of patience.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes patience as restraining oneself from sins, paired with worship and especially prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالصبر الكف عن المعاصي؛ ولهذا قرنه بأداء العبادات وأعلاها: فعل الصلاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r6.claim: Umar says patience under misfortune is good, but greater patience is keeping away from God's prohibitions; Hasan al-Basri reports similarly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r6.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب، رضي الله عنه، قال: الصبر صبران: صبر عند المصيبة حسن، وأحسن منه الصبر عن محارم الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r7.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr defines patience as acknowledging what has happened as God's decree, accounting it with God, and hoping for reward; outward composure can hide inner distress.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: الصبر اعتراف العبد لله بما أصاب فيه، واحتسابه عند الله ورجاء ثوابه، وقد يجزع الرجل وهو يتجلد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r8.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r8.claim: Abu al-Aliya says patience and prayer help one seek God's good pleasure and recognize that both are obedience to Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r8.anchor: وقال أبو العالية في قوله: {واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة} على مرضاة الله، واعلموا أنها من طاعة الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r9.claim: Prayer is one of the greatest aids to steadfastness; 29:45 says it restrains indecency and wrong, while remembrance of God is greater.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r9.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {اتل ما أوحي إليك من الكتاب وأقم الصلاة إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر ولذكر الله أكبر}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r10.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r10.claim: Hudhayfa reports that when a matter distressed the Prophet, he prayed; Ahmad transmits the report, also given by Abu Dawud.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251#2/r10.anchor: قال حذيفة، يعني ابن اليمان: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا حزبه أمر صلى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r1.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r1.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits Hudhayfa's report that when anything distressed the Prophet, he turned to prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r1.anchor: عن حذيفة، قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا حزبه أمر فزع إلى الصلاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r2.speaker: عبد العزيز ابن أخي حذيفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r2.claim: A version is sent through Abd al-Aziz, Hudhayfa's nephew or brother, as a disconnected report: the Prophet prayed wrapped in a cloak on the night of the Confederates and prayed whenever distressed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r2.anchor: رجعت إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة الأحزاب وهو مشتمل في شملة يصلي، وكان إذا حزبه أمر صلى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r3.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r3.claim: Ali says that on the night of Badr everyone was asleep except the Prophet, who prayed and supplicated until morning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r3.anchor: سمع عليا يقول: لقد رأيتنا ليلة بدر وما فينا إلا نائم غير رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي ويدعو حتى أصبح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir reports that the Prophet told Abu Hurayra, who lay on his stomach with abdominal pain, to get up and pray, saying prayer is healing.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r5.claim: When told during travel that his brother Qutham had died, Ibn Abbas prayed two lengthy rak'ahs after dismounting, then continued his journey while reciting this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r5.anchor: أن ابن عباس نعي إليه أخوه قثم وهو في سفر، فاسترجع، ثم تنحى عن الطريق، فأناخ فصلى ركعتين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits Ibn Jurayj's explanation that patience and prayer are two aids for obtaining God's mercy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r6.anchor: وقال سنيد، عن حجاج، عن ابن جرير: {واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة} قال: إنهما معونتان على رحمة الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r7.claim: Mujahid says the feminine pronoun in وإنها refers to prayer, a reading Ibn Jarir also chooses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r7.anchor: والضمير في قوله: {وإنها} عائد إلى الصلاة، نص عليه مجاهد، واختاره ابن جرير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir also allows the pronoun to refer to the instruction to persevere in patience and prayer, comparing the way a trait or instruction is referenced in 28:80 and 41:34–35.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p252/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون عائدا على ما يدل عليه الكلام، وهو الوصية بذلك، كقوله تعالى في قصة قارون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the humble are those who affirm what God revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r1.anchor: قال ابن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: يعني المصدقين بما أنزل الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies the humble as true believers.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the humble are those who fear God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r3.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: إلا على الخاشعين الخائفين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r4.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan explains the humble as the lowly and meek.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان: إلا على الخاشعين يعني به المتواضعين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r5.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says prayer is heavy except for those who submit to God's obedience, fear His force, and affirm His promises and threats.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r5.anchor: وقال الضحاك: {وإنها لكبيرة} قال: إنها لثقيلة إلا على الخاضعين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir compares the difficulty being discussed to a hadith saying a tremendous matter is easy for the person whom God makes it easy for.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r6.anchor: في الحديث: "لقد سألت عن عظيم، وإنه ليسير على من يسره الله عليه"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r7.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r7.claim: Ibn Jarir reads the verse as telling People of Scripture to restrain themselves in God's obedience and establish prayer, which prevents wrongdoing and brings His pleasure; only the submissive find it easy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r7.anchor: وقال ابن جرير: معنى الآية: واستعينوا أيها الأحبار من أهل الكتاب، بحبس أنفسكم على طاعة الله وبإقامة الصلاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r8.claim: Although the passage warns Israel, Ibn Kathir says this command is not exclusive to them; it applies generally to them and others.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p253/r8.anchor: والظاهر أن الآية وإن كانت خطابا في سياق إنذار بني إسرائيل، فإنهم لم يقصدوا بها على سبيل التخصيص، وإنما هي عامة لهم، ولغيرهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p254/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p254/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p254/r1.claim: The people of humility find prayer or the counsel heavy only if they do not know they will meet God; the humble know they will be gathered before Him and return to His will and just judgment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p254/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {الذين يظنون أنهم ملاقو ربهم وأنهم إليه راجعون} هذا من تمام الكلام الذي قبله

NAHHAS:v1p220/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p220/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p220/r3.claim: The verse is an imperative and الصبر is genitive after باء. The best interpretation is patience in abstaining from sins, which is also patience in obedience.
NAHHAS:v1p220/r3.anchor: أمر ( بالصبر ) خفض بالباء قال أبو جعفر وقد ذكرنا فيه أقوالا

NAHHAS:v1p220/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p220/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p220/r4.claim: Absolute use of صابر means one who abstains from sins; someone enduring a particular calamity is described as patient over that specific thing.
NAHHAS:v1p220/r4.anchor: ولا يقال لمن صبر على المصيبة صابر إنما يقال صابر على كذا

NAHHAS:v1p220/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p220/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p220/r5.claim: The reward of the patient supports the interpretation of ṣabr as obedience and abstention from sin.
NAHHAS:v1p220/r5.anchor: إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب

NAHHAS:v1p220/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p220/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p220/r6.claim: الصلاة is coordinated as in the pairing of Gabriel and Michael.
NAHHAS:v1p220/r6.anchor: ويكون ( والصلاة ) مثل قوله وجبريل وميكال

NAHHAS:v1p220/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p220/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p220/r7.claim: إنها is parsed as إن with its noun and predicate; masculine singular or dual forms are possible outside Qurʾānic recitation.
NAHHAS:v1p220/r7.anchor: ( وإنها لكبيرة ) اسم إن وخبرها ويجوز في غير القرآن وأنه ويجوز وأنهما

JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r1.claim: Istiʿāna means asking for aid, and ṣabr is restraining the self from what it desires, opposite to panic; the cited poem contrasts patience with despair.
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r1.anchor: الاستعانة: طلب المعونة، يقال: استعان به فأعانه. والصبر: حبس النفس عما ينازع إليه

JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r2.claim: Ṣabūr describes someone who is very patient.

JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r3.speaker: ابن دريد
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r3.claim: Khushūʿ, khushūʿ-like submission, and humility are near-synonyms opposite to arrogance; khāshiʿ can mean poor, submissive, or—in some dialects—one who bows.
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r3.anchor: والخشوع والخضوع والتذلل نظائر، ونقيضه الاستكبار، يقال: خشع خشوعا

JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r4.claim: Some take the pronoun in innahā to refer to an expressed antecedent: prayer, seeking aid through both prayer and patience, or the whole preceding address, the last from Abū ʿAlī.
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r4.anchor: على الصلاة، وقيل: على الاستعانة، يعني أن الاستعانة بهما لكبيرة، وقيل: جميع ما تقدم ذكره

JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r5.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r5.claim: An unexpressed antecedent may be the response to the Prophet, but the source says this is not apt because it was neither mentioned nor uniquely implied.
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r5.anchor: قيل: على الإجابة للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عن الأصم، وليس بالوجه؛ لأنه لم يجر له ذكر

JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r6.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r6.claim: Other proposed implicit antecedents are self-discipline, what came before, or prayer and the kinds of patience, the last view attributed to the judge.
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: أراد مؤاخذة النفس بهما لكبيرة، وقيل: أراد به ما تقدم، وقيل: أراد الصلاة وضروب الصبر

JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r7.claim: Abū Muslim says the implicit antecedent is this deed, which is burdensome.
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: هذه الفعلة لكبيرة، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r8.claim: The singular pronoun may refer only to prayer, singled out to emphasize its status, universal obligation, and importance.
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r8.anchor: أن المعنى على الصلاة دون غيرها على ظاهر الكلام، وخصها بالذكر لتأكيد حالها وعموم فرضها

JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r9.claim: Alternatively it can mean performing both, despite the singular form, like the verse saying God and His Messenger are more entitled to please them.
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r9.anchor: أن المراد به الإتيان بهما، وإن كان اللفظ على الواحد كقوله: (والله ورسوله أحق أن يرضوه)

JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r10.speaker: الأخفش
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash says the singular refers distributively to each of the two, each being burdensome.
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r10.anchor: الثالث: أراد كل خصلة منهما لكبيرة، عن الأخفش

JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r11.claim: A further analysis refers the pronoun to istiʿāna, the most apparent and general antecedent; Arabic uses the same construction for gold and silver with a singular pronoun.
JISHUMI:v1p361#2/r11.anchor: الرابع: يعود إلى الاستعانة، قيل: إنها تعود على الأظهر والأعم، ومن شأن العرب تفعل ذلك

JISHUMI:v1p363/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p363/r1.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p363/r1.claim: The address is said to be directed to Jews; Abū ʿAlī instead says it turns to Muslims, but the Jewish address is more apparent from the surrounding context.
JISHUMI:v1p363/r1.anchor: قيل: إنه خطاب لليهود، وفيهم نزل، وقيل: رجع بهذا القول إلى المسلمين، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v1p363/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p363/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p363/r2.claim: God commands seeking help through obedience in carrying out what He required.
JISHUMI:v1p363/r2.anchor: ثم أمر تعالى بالاستعانة بطاعته تعالى على أداء ما كلف

JISHUMI:v1p363/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p363/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p363/r3.claim: The omitted object of seeking help can be the previously mentioned duties such as prayer and almsgiving and refraining from prohibitions.
JISHUMI:v1p363/r3.anchor: والمراد على أداء الفرائض التي تقدم ذكرها من الصلاة والزكاة وغيرهما، وعن الانتهاء عما نهوا عنه

JISHUMI:v1p363/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p363/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p363/r4.claim: Another view addresses Jews taking bribes from their followers to alter religion and tells them to seek relief rather than do so.
JISHUMI:v1p363/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو خطاب لليهود الذين أخذوا الرشا من أتباعهم على تغيير الدين

JISHUMI:v1p363/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p363/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p363/r5.claim: Other proposed objects are the hardship of religious duties, fulfilling the covenant of obedience in their scripture, or carrying out what was promised to those who follow the messengers, according to Abū Muslim.
JISHUMI:v1p363/r5.anchor: وقيل: على مشقة التكليف، وقيل على الوفاء بعهدي الذي عاهدتموني في كتابكم من طاعتي

JISHUMI:v1p363/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p363/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p363/r6.claim: Prayer aids obedience through Qur’an recitation, reflection, admonition, action, supplication, humility, resisting arrogance and worldly love, and avoiding indecency and wrongdoing.
JISHUMI:v1p363/r6.anchor: أما الصلاة فلما فيها من تلاوة القرآن والتدبر في معانيه والاتعاظ بمواعظه، والإقدام على أوامره

JISHUMI:v1p363/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p363/r7.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p363/r7.claim: Ṣabr is interpreted as fasting, abstaining from forbidden acts, or persevering in obedience and avoiding sin.
JISHUMI:v1p363/r7.anchor: فأما الصبر فقيل: أراد به الصوم وقيل: الكف عن المحارم، وقيل: الصبر على الطاعة وعن المعصية

JISHUMI:v1p363/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p363/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p363/r8.claim: Another explanation sees patience and prayer as divine aids that draw people to obedience and away from sin.
JISHUMI:v1p363/r8.anchor: وجه آخر: أن الصبر والصلاة ألطاف في الدعاء إلى الطاعات واجتناب المعاصي

JISHUMI:v1p363/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p363/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p363/r9.claim: A further explanation pairs patience as the greatest act of the heart with prayer as the greatest act of the limbs.
JISHUMI:v1p363/r9.anchor: ليس من أفعال القلب أعظم من الصبر ولا في أفعال الجوارح أعظم من الصلاة

JISHUMI:v1p363/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p363/r10.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
JISHUMI:v1p363/r10.claim: Kabīra means heavy or burdensome, since people liken difficult burdens to heavy bodies.
JISHUMI:v1p363/r10.anchor: أي ثقيلة عن الحسن وجماعة، والأصل فيه أن ما يكبر يثقل على الإنسان حمله

JISHUMI:v1p363/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p363/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p363/r11.claim: Al-khāshiʿīn may mean those who pray.
JISHUMI:v1p363/r11.anchor: قيل: على المصلين، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v1p363/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p363/r12.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p363/r12.claim: Abū ʿAlī interprets al-khāshiʿīn as believers.

JISHUMI:v1p363/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p363/r13.speaker: الحسن والأصم
JISHUMI:v1p363/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Aṣamm interpret al-khāshiʿīn as those who fear.

JISHUMI:v1p363/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p363/r14.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v1p363/r14.claim: Muqātil interprets al-khāshiʿīn as the humble.

JISHUMI:v1p363/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p363/r15.speaker: أبو روق
JISHUMI:v1p363/r15.claim: Abū Rawq interprets al-khāshiʿīn as the obedient.

JISHUMI:v1p363/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p363/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p363/r16.claim: The source raises an objection: if prayer and patience are not burdensome to the humble, how do they merit reward?
JISHUMI:v1p363/r16.anchor: فإذا لم يكبر عليه، كيف يستحق الثواب؟

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r1.claim: Ṣabr is restraining the self from what it desires; a bereaved person restrains grief, and fasting restrains food and drink, so Ramadan is called the month of patience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r1.anchor: أما الصبر : فهو حبس النفس عما تنازع إليه , ومنه صبر صاحب المصيبة , أن يحبس نفسه عن الجزع , وسمي الصوم صبرا لحبس النفس عن الطعام والشراب

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r2.claim: A hadith says to kill the killer and detain the person who held the victim while another killed him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r2.anchor: وجاء في الحديث : ( اقتلوا القاتل , واصبروا الصابر ) وذلك فيمن أمسك رجلا حتى قتله آخر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r3.claim: The commanded patience may be steadfastness in obedience and restraint from disobedience, or it may mean fasting.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r3.anchor: وفي الصبر المأمور به , قولان : أحدهما : أنه الصبر على طاعته , والكف عن معصيته . والثاني : أنه الصوم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r4.claim: When something distressed him, the Prophet sought help through prayer and fasting.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r4.anchor: وقد كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا حزبه أمر استعان بالصلاة والصيام

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r5.claim: A report says the Prophet saw Salman face down; when Salman complained of cold, the Prophet told him to rise and pray, saying prayer heals.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r5.anchor: وروي أنه رأى سلمان منبطحا على وجهه , فقال له : أشكو من برد . قال : ( قم فصل الصلاة تشف )

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r6.claim: The feminine pronoun in “it is difficult” may refer to prayer, the nearest feminine word, making prayer heavy except for believers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r6.anchor: يعني : وإن الصلاة لثقيلة إلا على المؤمنين , لعود الكناية إلى مؤنث اللفظ

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r7.claim: It may refer to patience and prayer together, though the feminine pronoun returns to prayer as the nearest antecedent; the cited line likewise predicates a singular verb of two subjects.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r7.anchor: يعني الصبر والصلاة , فأرادهما , وإن عادت الكناية إلى الصلاة ؛ لأنها أقرب مذكور

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r8.claim: A third interpretation says responding to Muhammad is difficult except for the humble.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r8.anchor: والثالث : وإن إجابة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لشديدة إلا على الخاشعين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r9.claim: Khushūʿ means humility before God; one distinction says khudūʿ is bodily submission, while khushūʿ appears in voice and sight.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#3/r9.anchor: والخشوع في الله : التواضع , ونظيره الخضوع , وقيل : إن الخضوع في البدن , والخشوع في الصوت , والبصر

MUJAHID:v1p74#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p74#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p74#2/r1.claim: The truly humble people on whom prayer is not burdensome are the believers in truth.
MUJAHID:v1p74#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ إلا على الخاشعين ﴾ يقول إلا على المؤمنين حقا

MUQATIL:2:44-46/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:44-46/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:44-46/r3.claim: Seeking help for the Hereafter means patiently observing the obligations and guarding the five prayers at their appointed times.

MUQATIL:2:44-46/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:44-46/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:44-46/r4.claim: The qibla change from Jerusalem to the Kaaba was burdensome for Jews including Jaddi ibn Akhtab and Saʿid ibn ʿAmr the poet, but not for humble believers.
MUQATIL:2:44-46/r4.anchor: فكبر ذلك على اليهود منهم: جدى بن أخطب، وسعيد بن عمرو الشاعر وغيرهم،

MUQATIL:2:44-46/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:44-46/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:44-46/r5.claim: The humble are believing people for whom the qibla change was not difficult; they know with certainty that they will meet their Lord in the Hereafter and return to Him for recompense.
MUQATIL:2:44-46/r5.anchor: يعنى إلا على المتواضعين من المؤمنين، لم يكبر عليهم تحويل القبلة،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r1.claim: Seek God's help for your needs by combining patience with prayer and patiently bearing prayer's duties, sincerity, distractions, etiquette and humility while knowing one stands before the Lord of heaven and earth.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r1.anchor: تصلوا صابرين على تكاليف الصلاة محتملين لمشاقها وما يجب فيها من إخلاص القلب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r2.claim: Another application is to endure calamities and turn to prayer when they occur; the Prophet used to resort to prayer when distressed.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r2.anchor: بالصبر عليها والالتجاء إلى الصلاة عند وقوعها وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا حزبه أمر فزع إلى الصلاة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r3.claim: When his brother Qutham died while Ibn Abbas was travelling, he said the words of return to God, prayed two rakahs, and invoked this command.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما أنه نعى إليه أخوه وقثم وهو فى سفر فاسترجع وصلى ركعتين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r4.claim: One interpretation takes patience to mean fasting, since fasting restrains one from things that break the fast and Ramadan is called the month of patience.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r4.anchor: وقيل الصبر الصوم لأنه حبس عن المفطرات ومنه قيل لشهر رمضان شهر الصبر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes prayer to mean supplication: endure affliction and implore God to remove it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r5.anchor: وقيل الصلاة الدعاء أي استعينوا على البلايا بالصبر والإلتجاء إلى الدعاء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r6.claim: The feminine pronoun in the next clause may refer either to prayer or to seeking help.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r7.claim: Prayer or seeking help is burdensome in the sense of difficult and heavy, but not for the humble.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r7.anchor: لشاقة ثقيلة من قولك كبر على هذا الأمر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r8.claim: The humble find it easier because they expect the reward stored up for those who bear its hardships.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#4/r8.anchor: لأنهم يتوقعون ما ادخر للصابرين على متاعبها فتهون عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r1.claim: Ṣabr means restraint: killing an animal ṣabran means holding it until it dies, and the prohibited maṣbūra is an animal kept as a target.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r1.anchor: الصبر: الحبس في اللغة. وقتل فلان صبرا أي أمسك وحبس حتى أتلف.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r2.speaker: عنترة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r2.claim: ʿAntara’s verse illustrates steadfast endurance: the speaker remains firmly planted while the coward’s soul rises in fear.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r2.anchor: وقال عنترة: فصبرت عارفة لذلك حرة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r3.claim: Qurtubi says the command covers patience in obedience and abstaining from disobedience; refraining from sin entails patience in obedience too, the soundest view.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r3.anchor: أمر تعالى بالصبر على الطاعة وعن المخالفة في كتابه فقال: «واصبروا». يقال: فلان صابر عن المعاصي وإذا صبر عن المعاصي فقد صبر على الطاعة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r4.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r4.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says one should not call someone simply patient about a sin; an unrestricted description of patience means the virtuous kind just described.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r4.anchor: قال النحاس: ولا يقال لمن صبر على المعصية: صابر إنما يقال: صابر على كذا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r5.claim: Prayer is singled out among acts of worship to honor it; when distressed, the Prophet turned to ritual prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r5.anchor: خص الصلاة بالذكر من بين سائر العبادات تنويها بذكره.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r6.claim: While traveling, Ibn ʿAbbās received news of his brother Qutham’s death, or alternatively his daughter’s; he consoled himself, prayed, and recited this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r6.anchor: ومنه ما روي أن عبد الله بن عباس نعي له أخوه قثم وقيل بنت له وهو في سفر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r7.claim: On this interpretation, al-ṣalāt means the prescribed ritual prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r7.anchor: فالصلاة على هذا التأويل هي الشرعية.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r8.claim: Some say ṣalāt means supplication in its ordinary Arabic sense, aligning the verse with the command to stand firm and remember God when meeting an army.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r8.anchor: وقال قوم: هي الدعاء على عرفها في اللغة فتكون الآية على هذا التأويل مشبهة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r9.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r9.claim: Mujāhid interprets ṣabr as fasting, called Ramadan the month of patience; fasting restrains desire and worldly attachment, while prayer restrains indecency, humbles, and recalls the afterlife through Quran recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r9.anchor: الصبر في هذه الآية الصوم ومنه قيل لرمضان: شهر الصبر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r10.claim: Enduring harm and obedience is the struggle of the self: curbing desires and excess, a trait of prophets and the righteous.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r10.anchor: الصبر على الأذى والطاعات من باب جهاد النفس وقمعها عن شهواتها ومنعها من تطاولها، وهو من أخلاق الأنبياء والصالحين.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r11.speaker: يحيى بن اليمان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r11.claim: Yaḥyā ibn al-Yamān defines patience as not wishing for a state beyond one’s provision and accepting God’s decree in worldly and otherworldly affairs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r11.anchor: قال يحيى بن اليمان: الصبر ألا تتمنى حالة سوى ما رزقك الله، والرضا بما قضى الله من أمر دنياك وآخرتك.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r12.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r12.claim: Al-Shaʿbī reports ʿAlī saying patience stands to faith as the head to the body; al-Ṭabarī agrees because faith includes heart, tongue, and bodily action, requiring perseverance.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45/r12.anchor: وقال الشعبي: قال علي رضي الله عنه: الصبر من الإيمان بمنزلة الرأس من الجسد.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r1.claim: Good deeds usually receive tenfold reward and charity receives more, but the patient are paid without measure and praised for endurance and forgiveness.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r1.anchor: من جآء بالحسنة فله عشر أمثالها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r2.claim: Some interpret ‘the patient’ in the promise of unmeasured reward as those who fast, since a Prophetic report says fasting belongs to God and He rewards it without specifying a measure.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r2.anchor: أي الصائمون لقوله تعالى في صحيح السنة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r3.claim: Abū Mūsā reports the Prophet saying none is more forbearing toward hurtful speech than God: people attribute a child to Him, yet He continues to pardon and provide; al-Bukhārī transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r3.anchor: كما في حديث أبي موسى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r4.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r4.claim: The scholars explain God’s ṣabr as ḥilm: delaying punishment of those who deserve it; the attribute occurs in hadith, not Quran, and Sunnis interpret it as forbearance, as Ibn Fūrak and others say; al-Ṣabūr is its emphatic name.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r4.anchor: قال علماؤنا: وصف الله تعالى بالصبر إنما هو بمعنى الحلم، ومعنى وصفه تعالى بالحلم هو تأخير العقوبة عن المستحقين لها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r5.claim: One view returns ‘it is surely hard’ only to prayer: prayer restrains all limbs and desires, while fasting restricts some appetites but leaves other pleasures available, making prayer harder on the self.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r5.anchor: اختلف المتأولون في عود الضمير من قوله: «وإنها» فقيل: على الصلاة وحدها خاصة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r6.claim: Another view says the pronoun refers to both patience and prayer, but uses the dominant term, prayer, for both.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: عليهما، ولكنه كنى عن الأغلب وهو الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r1.claim: The feminine pronoun may return to silver in 9:34 because it is more prevalent, and to trade in 62:11 because it is more important.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r1.anchor: فرد الكناية إلى الفضة لأنها الأغلب والأعم، وإلى التجارة لأنها الأفضل والأهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r2.claim: One view makes the pronoun refer to prayer because patience is included in it, as the Messenger's approval is included in God's approval.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r2.anchor: إن الصبر لما كان داخلا في الصلاة أعاد عليها كما قال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r3.claim: Another view refers it to both patience and prayer but omits the dual ending for brevity, as in the verse about Mary and her son and the cited poetry.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r3.anchor: رد الكناية إلى كل واحد منهما لكن حذف اختصارا قال الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r4.claim: The pronoun may refer to worship, which patience and prayer encompass in meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r4.anchor: على العبادة التي يتضمنها بالمعنى ذكر الصبر والصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r5.claim: It may refer to the verbal noun seeking help, implied by the command to seek help.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r5.anchor: على المصدر، وهي الاستعانة التي يقتضيها قوله: { واستعينوا }

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r6.claim: It may refer to Muhammad's response, since patience and prayer were among the matters he called people to.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r6.anchor: على إجابة محمد عليه السلام لأن الصبر والصلاة مما كان يدعو إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r7.claim: It may refer to the Kaaba, since prayer is commanded toward it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r7.anchor: على الكعبة لأن الأمر بالصلاة إنما هو إليها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r8.claim: Kabīrah means heavy and difficult and is the predicate of inna; a non-Qur'anic form could use the masculine pronoun.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r8.anchor: { وكبيرة } معناه ثقيلة شاقة، خبر «إن». ويجوز في غير القرآن: وإنه لكبيرة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r9.claim: Prayer is light for the humble; the masters of spiritual meanings say they are people supported from eternity by election and guidance.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r9.anchor: { إلا على الخاشعين } فإنها خفيفة عليهم. قال أرباب المعاني

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r10.claim: Khashiʿūn means humble people; khushūʿ is an inward state that appears in the limbs as stillness and humility.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r10.anchor: الخاشعون جمع خاشع وهو المتواضع. والخشوع: هيئة في النفس يظهر منها في الجوارح سكون وتواضع.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r11.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r11.claim: Qatādah locates khushūʿ in the heart as fear, with lowering the gaze during prayer as its outward sign.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة: الخشوع في القلب، وهو الخوف وغض البصر في الصلاة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r12.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r12.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the humble person visibly shows abasement, like a house made desolate after its inhabitants leave.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r12.anchor: قال الزجاج: الخاشع الذي يرى أثر الذل والخشوع عليه كخشوع الدار بعد الإقواء.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r13.speaker: النابغة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r13.claim: Al-Nābighah's line uses khāshiʿ for an old dwelling's worn, quiet appearance, illustrating the root's basic sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#3/r13.anchor: قال النابغة: رماد ككحل العين لأيا أبينه ونؤي كجذم الحوض أثلم خاشع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r1.claim: The root describes an obscure place and quiet voices; khashʿah is a soft piece of land, and a khāshiʿ town is dusty and uninhabited.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r1.anchor: ومكان خاشع: لا يهتدى له. وخشعت الأصوات أي سكنت.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r2.claim: Other lexical senses are sticky sputum in the chest and lowering the gaze; a hadith calls a soft patch on water a khashʿah before it was spread out.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r2.anchor: وخشعت خراشي صدره إذا ألقى بصاقا لزجا. وخشع ببصره إذا غضه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r3.speaker: الأعمش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r3.claim: Al-Aʿmash rebuked Sufyān for seeking leadership without understanding khushūʿ and rejected rough food, rough clothes, and a bowed head as its definition.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r3.anchor: سألت الأعمش عن الخشوع فقال: يا ثوري، أنت تريد أن تكون إماما للناس ولا تعرف الخشوع!

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r4.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r4.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī defines khushūʿ as treating noble and lowly alike in matters of right and humbling oneself to God in every duty.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r4.anchor: لكن الخشوع أن ترى الشريف والدنيء في الحق سواء، وتخشع لله في كل فرض افترض عليك.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r5.claim: ʿUmar told a youth who had lowered his head to raise it, since outward posture cannot add to what is in the heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r5.anchor: يا هذا! ارفع رأسك، فإن الخشوع لا يزيد على ما في القلب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r6.claim: ʿAlī says khushūʿ is in the heart, includes gentleness toward a Muslim, and means not turning during prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r6.anchor: الخشوع في القلب، وأن تلين كفيك للمرء المسلم، وألا تلتفت في صلاتك.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r7.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says the fuller treatment will come with the description of believers who are humble in prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r7.anchor: وسيأتي هذا المعنى مجودا عند قوله تعالى: قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r8.claim: Displaying more humility to people than exists in the heart is hypocrisy added to hypocrisy.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r8.anchor: فمن أظهر للناس خشوعا فوق ما في قلبه فإنما أظهر نفاقا على نفاق.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r9.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r9.claim: Sahl says none is truly humble until every hair is humbled, citing the verse about believers' skins shivering.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r9.anchor: قال سهل بن عبد الله: لا يكون خاشعا حتى تخشع كل شعرة على جسده

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r10.claim: Al-Qurṭubī calls heart-born fear the praised khushūʿ: it compels unfeigned outward composure and submission; the early generations tried to conceal its visible signs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r10.anchor: هذا هو الخشوع المحمود لأن الخوف إذا سكن القلب أوجب خشوع الظاهر فلا يملك صاحبه دفعه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r11.claim: Feigning humility through affected tears or a bowed head to win esteem is blameworthy deception from Satan and self-delusion.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r11.anchor: وأما المذموم فتكلفه والتباكي ومطأطأة الرأس كما يفعله الجهال ليروا بعين البر والإجلال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r12.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r12.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that ʿUmar jabbed or punched a man who sighed theatrically as if pretending to grieve.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r12.anchor: روى الحسن أن رجلا تنفس عند عمر بن الخطاب كأنه يتحازن فلكزه عمر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r13.claim: Al-Qurṭubī describes ʿUmar as audible when speaking, quick when walking, forceful when striking, a genuine ascetic and truly humble man.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r13.anchor: وكان عمر رضي الله عنه إذا تكلم أسمع، وإذا مشى أسرع، وإذا ضرب أوجع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r14.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r14.claim: Mujāhid, transmitted by Ibn Abī Najīḥ, says the humble are the true believers.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:45#4/r14.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال: الخاشعون هم المؤمنون حقا.

RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r1.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r1.claim: Some hold that the address to seek help through patience and prayer is to believers in Muhammad, since deniers of prayer and patience in his religion would not be addressed this way.
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r1.anchor: فقال قوم : هم المؤمنون بالرسول قال لأن من ينكر الصلاة أصلا والصبر على دين محمد

RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r2.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r2.claim: This view allows the discourse to begin by addressing Israelites and then shift to believers in Muhammad.
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r2.anchor: ولا يمتنع أن يكون الخطاب أولا في بني إسرائيل ثم يقع بعد ذلك خطابا للمؤمنين

RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r3.claim: Razi considers Israelites the likelier audience because assigning the address to another group would disrupt the passage's coherence.
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r3.anchor: والأقرب أن المخاطبين هم بنو إسرائيل لأن صرف الخطاب إلى غيرهم يوجب تفكيك النظم

RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r4.speaker: معترض
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r4.claim: An objection asks how Israelites can be ordered to patience and prayer if they reject both.
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r4.anchor: فإن قيل كيف يؤمرون بالصبر والصلاة مع كونهم منكرين لهما

RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r5.claim: Razi denies that they rejected the shared meaning: everyone knows patience in what requires patience is good, and prayer humbles one before the Creator and consoles against worldly distress; only its manner differs between Jewish and Muslim prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r5.anchor: لا نسلم كونهم منكرين لهما ؛ وذلك لأن كل أحد يعلم أن الصبر على ما يجب الصبر عليه حسن

RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r6.claim: Because the command concerns the common essence of prayer and patience rather than their differing forms, the objection disappears.
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r6.anchor: وإذا كان متعلق الأمر هو الماهية التي هي القدر المشترك زال الإشكال المذكور

RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r7.claim: After ordering faith, abandoning misguidance, and observing laws such as prayer and almsgiving, God prescribes patience and prayer as a remedy because giving up status, wealth, and prestige is difficult.
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r7.anchor: لما أمرهم بالإيمان وبترك الإضلال وبالتزام الشرائع وهي الصلاة والزكاة ، وكان ذلك شاقا عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r8.claim: One explanation takes patience as restraining the self from pleasures while accepting Muhammad's religion; habituation makes this easier, and prayer's remembrance of God's majesty, power, mercy, and favor inclines one to obey and avoid sin.
RAZI-FULL:v3p46/r8.anchor: واستعينوا على ترك ما تحبون من الدنيا والدخول فيما تستثقله طباعكم من قبول دين محمد

RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r1.claim: A second explanation takes patience to mean fasting: abstaining from food, drink, and sexual desire weakens attachment to worldly life, and with prayer it illuminates the heart with knowledge of God.
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r1.anchor: المراد من الصبر ههنا هو الصوم لأن الصائم صابر عن الطعام والشراب

RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r2.claim: Fasting precedes prayer because fasting removes what is undesirable while prayer brings what is desirable, and negation precedes affirmation.
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r2.anchor: لأن تأثير الصوم في إزالة ما لا ينبغي وتأثير الصلاة في حصول ما ينبغي والنفي مقدم على الإثبات

RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r3.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r3.claim: The Prophet said that fasting is a shield against the Fire.
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r3.anchor: ولأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال الصوم جنة من النار

RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r4.claim: Prayer prevents indecency and wrongdoing, turns one from worldly occupation, humbles the heart, and through recitation and reflection on promises, warnings, and the afterlife makes renouncing worldly leadership easier.
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r4.anchor: لأن الصلاة تمنع عن الاشتغال بالدنيا وتخشع القلب ويحصل بسببها تلاوة الكتاب

RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r5.claim: A parallel command to seek help through patience and prayer appears in the address to believers, with God's support for the patient.

RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r6.claim: Razi gives three possible referents for the feminine pronoun: prayer, the implied act of seeking help, or all the commands and prohibitions addressed to Israel from remembering God's favor through this verse.
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r6.anchor: أما قوله تعالى { وإنها } ففي هذا الضمير وجوه أحدها : الضمير عائد إلى الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r7.claim: Arabic can omit a noun and refer to it by implication when the hearer understands it; Razi gives examples referring implicitly to earth and a city, as does the verse about God not leaving any creature on it.
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r7.anchor: والعرب قد تضمر الشيء اختصارا أو تقتصر فيه على الإيماء إذا وثقت بعلم المخاطب

RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r8.claim: Great means arduous: prayer is hard for those lacking humility but easy for the humble.
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r8.anchor: أي لشاقة ثقيلة على هؤلاء سهلة على الخاشعين

RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r9.speaker: معترض
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r9.claim: An objection says this implies the humble bear the greater burden, since they engage their bodies, hearts, hearing, and sight, reflect on their words, and feel grief at warnings and hope at promises.
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r9.anchor: وكيف يكون ذلك والخاشع يستعمل عند الصلاة جوارحه وقلبه وسمعه وبصره

RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r10.claim: Razi clarifies that he does not mean prayer entails more exertion for the humble; it is hard for those who believe in neither reward for doing it nor punishment for leaving it.
RAZI-FULL:v3p46#2/r10.anchor: ليس المراد أن الذي يلحقهم من التعب أكثر مما يلحق الخاشع

RAZI-FULL:v3p47/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p47/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p47/r1.claim: An unbeliever finds prayer burdensome because he sees no benefit, whereas a monotheist expects great benefit from it and harm from neglecting it, so expected reward and escape from punishment make it easier.
RAZI-FULL:v3p47/r1.anchor: أما الموحد فلما اعتقد في فعلها أعظم المنافع وفي تركها أعظم المضار لم يثقل ذلك عليه

RAZI-FULL:v3p47/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p47/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p47/r2.claim: Prayer's difficulty is like bitter medicine: a sick person finds it easy if convinced it will cure him, and difficult without that belief.
RAZI-FULL:v3p47/r2.anchor: إذا قيل للمريض كل هذا الشيء المر فإن اعتقد أنه له فيه شفاء سهل ذلك عليه

RAZI-FULL:v3p47/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p47/r3.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v3p47/r3.claim: The Prophet described prayer as the coolness of his eyes; Razi says this follows from its benefits, not from prayer being burdensome to him, since he prayed until his feet swelled.
RAZI-FULL:v3p47/r3.anchor: وجعلت قرة عيني في الصلاة وصف الصلاة بذلك للوجوه التي ذكرناها

RAZI-FULL:v3p47/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p47/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p47/r4.claim: Razi defines humility as abasement and submission.

STUDYQURAN:2:45/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:45/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:45/r1.claim: This verse echoes 2:153; the Qurʾān also links patience with steadfastness in hardship and good through 12:18, 16:127, 23:111, 70:5, 90:17, and 103:3.

STUDYQURAN:2:45/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:45/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:45/r2.claim: Ṣabr means both enduring hardship and remaining steadfast in good.
STUDYQURAN:2:45/r2.anchor: ṣabr, like “patience,” means both the endurance of hardship and steadfastness in good.

STUDYQURAN:2:45/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:45/r3.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:45/r3.claim: The pronoun translated “this” may refer to prayer alone or to the whole admonition; the matter is difficult because it demands attention by day and night.
STUDYQURAN:2:45/r3.anchor: This—translating a pronoun denoting prayer or the admonition as a whole (IK)—is difficult

STUDYQURAN:2:45/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:45/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:45/r4.claim: Patience can be practiced through deferred gratification, whereas prayer requires retreating from the world and diminishing the ego.
STUDYQURAN:2:45/r4.anchor: one can be patient through the commonplace discipline of deferred gratification, whereas prayer always demands, in some measure, a retreat from the world and a diminution of the ego.

TAB-FULL:v1p617/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r1.claim: Al-Tabari says prayer helps people leave worldly life and its allure through recitation of scripture.
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r1.anchor: قيل: إن الصلاة فيها تلاوة كتاب الله، الداعية آياته إلى رفض الدنيا وهجر نعيمها

TAB-FULL:v1p617/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r2.claim: Al-Tabari rejects limiting patience here to fasting: fasting is one form of patience, while the command means enduring disliked obedience and restraining oneself from sin and desire.
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r2.anchor: والصوم بعض معاني الصبر عندنا. بل تأويل ذلك عندنا

TAB-FULL:v1p617/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r3.claim: Al-Tabari explains ṣabr as restraining the self from what it wants: the bereaved restrains grief and the Ramadan faster abstains from food and drink.
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r3.anchor: وأصل الصبر: منع النفس محابها وكفها عن هواها ولذلك قيل للصابر على المصيبة: صابر، لكفه نفسه عن الجزع

TAB-FULL:v1p617/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r4.claim: Al-Tabari says prayer's recitation urges rejection of worldly life and consoles people against its allure.
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r4.anchor: إن الصلاة فيها تلاوة كتاب الله، الداعية آياته إلى رفض الدنيا وهجر نعيمها، المسلية النفوس عن زينتها وغرورها

TAB-FULL:v1p617/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r5.speaker: حذيفة
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r5.claim: Hudhayfa reports that whenever a matter distressed the Prophet, he resorted to prayer.
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r5.anchor: عن حذيفة، قال: «كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، إذا حزبه أمر فزع إلى الصلاة»

TAB-FULL:v1p617/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r6.speaker: حذيفة
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r6.claim: In another report from Hudhayfa, the Prophet prayed when a matter distressed him.
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r6.anchor: قال حذيفة: «كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا حزبه أمر صلى»

TAB-FULL:v1p617/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r7.claim: Al-Tabari relates that the Prophet saw Abu Hurayra lying on his stomach, asked about pain, and told him to pray because prayer is healing.
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r7.anchor: عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه رأى أبا هريرة منبطحا على بطنه فقال له: «اشكنب درد» ؟ قال: نعم، قال: «قم فصل فإن في الصلاة شفاء»

TAB-FULL:v1p617/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r8.claim: Al-Tabari links the command to Muhammad's instruction to be patient with what people say and glorify God through the day and night.
TAB-FULL:v1p617/r8.anchor: كما أمر نبيه محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم بذلك، فقال له: {فاصبر} [طه: 130] يا محمد

TAB-FULL:v1p620/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p620/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p620/r1.claim: Patience and prayer help the People of the Book keep God's covenant through obedience, following Muhammad, and relinquishing leadership and worldly attachment.
TAB-FULL:v1p620/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية: " {واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة} [البقرة: 45] قال يقول: استعينوا بالصبر والصلاة على مرضاة الله، واعلموا أنهما من طاعة الله "

TAB-FULL:v1p620/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p620/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p620/r2.claim: When told of his brother Qutham's death while travelling, Ibn Abbas prayed two long-seated rakʿas and recited this verse for help.
TAB-FULL:v1p620/r2.anchor: أن ابن عباس: " نعي إليه أخوه قثم وهو في سفر، فاسترجع ثم تنحى عن الطريق، فأناخ فصلى ركعتين

TAB-FULL:v1p620/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p620/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v1p620/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya says patience and prayer aid people in seeking God's good pleasure and are acts of obedience to Him.
TAB-FULL:v1p620/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية: " {واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة} [البقرة: 45] قال يقول: استعينوا بالصبر والصلاة على مرضاة الله، واعلموا أنهما من طاعة الله "

TAB-FULL:v1p620/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p620/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v1p620/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj says patience and prayer are two aids toward receiving God's mercy.
TAB-FULL:v1p620/r4.anchor: قال ابن جريج: " في قوله: {واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة} [البقرة: 45] قال: إنهما معونتان على رحمة الله "

TAB-FULL:v1p620/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p620/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v1p620/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd reports that the polytheists called Muhammad's invitation to prayer and faith a great demand.
TAB-FULL:v1p620/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " في قوله: {واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة} [البقرة: 45] الآية، قال: قال المشركون: والله يا محمد إنك لتدعونا إلى أمر كبير

TAB-FULL:v1p621#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p621#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p621#2/r1.claim: Al-Tabari rejects an unsupported hidden interpretation and keeps to the apparent sense.
TAB-FULL:v1p621#2/r1.anchor: الكلام إلى باطن لا دلالة على صحته

TAB-FULL:v1p622/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p622/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p622/r1.claim: Al-Tabari glosses kabīra as severe and heavy.
TAB-FULL:v1p622/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك: " في قوله: {وإنها لكبيرة إلا على الخاشعين} [البقرة: 45] قال: إنها لثقيلة "

TAB-FULL:v1p622/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p622/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v1p622/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak likewise says that it is heavy.
TAB-FULL:v1p622/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك: " في قوله: {وإنها لكبيرة إلا على الخاشعين} [البقرة: 45] قال: إنها لثقيلة "

TAB-FULL:v1p623/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r1.claim: Al-Tabari says prayer is difficult except for those who are humble before God, obedient to Him, and afraid of Him.
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r1.anchor: إلا على المتواضعين لله المستكينين لطاعته المتذللين من مخافته

TAB-FULL:v1p623/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the humble as those who believe what God revealed.
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {إلا على الخاشعين} [البقرة: 45] يعني المصدقين بما أنزل الله "

TAB-FULL:v1p623/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya glosses the humble as those who fear.
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية: " في قوله: {إلا على الخاشعين} [البقرة: 45] قال: يعني الخائفين "

TAB-FULL:v1p623/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r4.claim: Mujahid identifies the humble as true believers.
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {إلا على الخاشعين} [البقرة: 45] قال: المؤمنين حقا "

TAB-FULL:v1p623/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd defines humility as fear and awe of God, citing people humbled by fear in another verse.
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " الخشوع: الخوف والخشية لله. وقرأ قول الله: {خاشعين من الذل} [الشورى: 45]

TAB-FULL:v1p623/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r6.claim: Al-Tabari gives the root sense of khushūʿ as humility, abasement, and submission; an anonymous poet's use of al-khashʿ for mountains illustrates being humbled by grief at al-Zubayr's loss.
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r6.anchor:
وأصل الخشوع: التواضع والتذلل والاستكانة ومنه قول الشاعر: [البحر الكامل]
لما أتى خبر الزبير تواضعت … سور المدينة والجبال الخشع

TAB-FULL:v1p623/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r7.claim: Al-Tabari concludes that the learned Israelites should restrain themselves from sin and establish prayer, which wards off indecency and wrongdoing; it is difficult only for the humble and submissive.
TAB-FULL:v1p623/r7.anchor: فمعنى الآية: واستعينوا أيها الأحبار من أهل الكتاب بحبس أنفسكم على طاعة الله، وكفها عن معاصي الله، وبإقامة الصلاة المانعة من الفحشاء والمنكر

TABATABAI:2:45-46/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:45-46/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:45-46/r1.claim: People seek aid when a task or calamity exceeds their individual strength; true aid comes only from God, through steadfastness and turning wholly toward Him in patience and prayer.
TABATABAI:2:45-46/r1.anchor: الاستعانة وهي طلب العون إنما يتم فيما لا يقوى الإنسان عليه وحده من المهمات والنوازل، وإذ لا معين في الحقيقة إلا الله سبحانه،

TABATABAI:2:45-46/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:45-46/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:45-46/r2.claim: Patience makes every great calamity seem smaller, while turning to God awakens faith and awareness of an unbreakable support; patience and prayer are the best means of help.
TABATABAI:2:45-46/r2.anchor: فالصبر يصغر كل عظيمة نازلة، وبالإقبال على الله والالتجاء إليه تستيقظ روح الإيمان،

TABATABAI:2:45-46/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:45-46/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:45-46/r3.claim: The feminine pronoun in 'it is hard' refers to prayer; referring it to seeking aid is unlikely because the exception for the humble fits prayer rather than patience or aid-seeking.
TABATABAI:2:45-46/r3.anchor: الضمير راجع إلى الصلاة، وأما إرجاعه إلى الاستعانة لتضمن قوله استعينوا ذلك

TABATABAI:2:45-46/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:45-46/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:45-46/r4.claim: Though both convey abasement, خضوع applies to the limbs while خشوع belongs to the heart.
TABATABAI:2:45-46/r4.anchor: والفرق بين الخشوع والخضوع مع أن في كليهما معنى التذلل، والانكسار أن الخضوع مختص بالجوارح والخشوع بالقلب.

TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r3.speaker: الصادق
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r3.claim: Al-Kafi reports that when Ali was troubled by a matter, he would rise to pray and recite this verse.
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r3.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام قال كان علي إذا أهاله أمر فزع قام إلى الصلاة ثم تلا هذه الآية

TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r4.speaker: الصادق
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r4.claim: In another al-Kafi report, patience is identified with fasting, and a person struck by a severe calamity is told to fast.
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r4.anchor: عنه عليه السلام في الآية، قال الصبر الصيام، وقال إذا نزلت بالرجل النازلة الشديدة فليصم.

TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r5.claim: Al-Tabari's al-Ayyashi also transmits the substance of both al-Kafi reports; fasting is an application of patience, not its exclusive meaning.
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r5.anchor: وروى مضمون الحديثين العياشي في تفسيره. وتفسير الصبر بالصيام من باب المصداق والجري.

TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r6.speaker: أبي الحسن
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r6.claim: Al-Ayyashi reports from Abu al-Hasan that patience is fasting: when hardship or calamity comes, one should fast; the humble are submissive and attentive in prayer, namely the Messenger and Ali.
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r6.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن أبي الحسن عليه السلام في الآية قال الصبر الصوم، إذا نزلت بالرجل الشدة أو النازلة فليصم،

TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī infers that fasting and prayer are recommended in calamities, as is seeking help through the Prophet and the wali; this allegorically interprets fasting and prayer as the Prophet and Ali.
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r7.anchor: قد استفاد عليه السلام استحباب الصوم والصلاة عند نزول الملمات والشدائد، وكذا التوسل بالنبي والولي عندها،

TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r9.speaker: الباقر
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r9.claim: Ibn Shahrashub transmits from al-Baqir that the verse was revealed about Ali, Uthman ibn Maz'un, Ammar ibn Yasir, and their companions.
TABATABAI:2:45-46#2/r9.anchor: وروى ابن شهراشوب عن الباقر عليه السلام أن الآية نازلة في علي وعثمان بن مظعون وعمار بن ياسر وأصحاب لهم.

ZAJJAJ:v1p125/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p125/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p125/r4.claim: Because the address concerns leaders among the People of the Book, prayer is prescribed to help them resist the desire for status: it recites what makes them value God’s reward over worldly life.
ZAJJAJ:v1p125/r4.anchor: وكانت لهم رئاسة عند أتباعهم فقيل لهم: استعينوا على ما يذهب عنكم شهوة الرياسة بالصلاة لأن الصلاة يتلى فيها ما يرغب فيما عند الله

ZAJJAJ:v1p125#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p125#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p125#2/r1.claim: Prayer joined with faith in the Prophet weighs heavily on unbelievers; the humble are those who submit, obey, and respond, without clinging to leadership at the cost of faith.
ZAJJAJ:v1p125#2/r1.anchor: إن الصلاة التي معها الإيمان بالنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كبيرة تكبر على الكفار وتعظم عليهم

ZAJJAJ:v1p125#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p125#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p125#2/r2.claim: The humble are those who submit, obey, and respond, since such a person does not cling to leadership after leaving disbelief for faith.
ZAJJAJ:v1p125#2/r2.anchor: والخاشع المتواضع المطيع المجيب لأن المتواضع لا يبالي برياسة كانت له مع كفر إذا انتقل إلى الإيمان.

TABRISI:2:45/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45/r1.claim: Ṣabr is restraining oneself from desires and impulses; patience in calamity restrains one from despair.
TABRISI:2:45/r1.anchor: الصبر منع النفس عن محابها وكفها عن هواها ومنه الصبر على المصيبة

TABRISI:2:45/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45/r2.claim: Ramadan is called the month of patience because a fasting person restrains himself from what would spoil the fast.

TABRISI:2:45/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45/r3.claim: Killing someone ṣabran means setting and holding the person for execution; the term also applies to a person held for killing or an oath, and ṣabbartuhu means making him swear by God with an emphatic oath.
TABRISI:2:45/r3.anchor: وقتل فلان صبرا وهو أن ينصب للقتل ويحبس عليه حتى يقتل وكل من حبسته لقتل أو يمين

TABRISI:2:45/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:2:45/r4.claim: A hadith commands killing the killer and confining the person who restrained the victim until the killer could act; no grading is stated.

TABRISI:2:45/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
