TABRISI:2:45/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45/r5.claim: Khushūʿ, submission, humility, and meekness are near-synonyms; arrogance is its opposite. Khushūʿ is in voice and sight, while khudūʿ is bodily submission.
TABRISI:2:45/r5.anchor: والخشوع والخضوع والتذلل والإخبات نظائر وضد الخشوع الاستكبار

TABRISI:2:45/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45/r6.claim: One khushūʿ-related verb describes lowering the gaze, another bowing the head; the Qur'an says eyes are humbled and voices subdued.
TABRISI:2:45/r6.anchor: وخشع الرجل إذا رمى ببصره إلى الأرض واختشع إذا طأطأ رأسه كالمتواضع

TABRISI:2:45/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45/r7.claim: Khāshiʿ, humble, meek, and subdued share a meaning; the word's root sense is softness and ease.
TABRISI:2:45/r7.anchor: وأصل الباء من اللين والسهولة والخاشع والمتواضع والمتذلل والمستكين بمعنى

TABRISI:2:45/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45/r8.claim: The poet says that when news of al-Zubayr arrived, the city's walls and meek mountains bowed, illustrating humility.
TABRISI:2:45/r8.anchor: لما أتى خبر الزبير تواضعت سور المدينة والجبال الخشع

TABRISI:2:45/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45/r9.claim: In ‘it is indeed burdensome,’ the emphatic lām moves to the predicate to separate it from inna; unlike inna, other sisters change the subject's grammatical category and do not take this lām.
TABRISI:2:45/r9.anchor: اللام تدخل في خبر إن ولا تدخل في خبر أخواتها لأنها لام التأكيد

TABRISI:2:45/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45/r10.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:2:45/r10.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the address is to Muslims.
TABRISI:2:45/r10.anchor: قال الجبائي إنه خطاب للمسلمين دون أهل الكتاب

TABRISI:2:45/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45/r11.speaker: الرماني وغيره
TABRISI:2:45/r11.claim: Al-Rummānī and others say the address is to the People of the Book and instructs believers as well.
TABRISI:2:45/r11.anchor: وقال الرماني وغيره هو خطاب لأهل الكتاب ويتناول المؤمنين على وجه التأديب

TABRISI:2:45/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45/r12.claim: The author prefers that the address concern all morally responsible people because there is no evidence for restricting it; context before and after supports the People of the Book.
TABRISI:2:45/r12.anchor: والأولى أن يكون خطابا لجميع المكلفين لفقد الدلالة على التخصيص

TABRISI:2:45/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45/r13.claim: On the People-of-the-Book reading, Jewish scholars' love of leadership kept them from following Muhammad, so they were told to endure hardship and seek help in fulfilling God's covenant through obedience and following His messenger.
TABRISI:2:45/r13.anchor: من قال إنه خطاب لليهود قال إن حب الرياسة كان تمنع علماء اليهود عن اتباع النبي

TABRISI:2:45/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45/r14.speaker: أئمتنا عليهم السلام
TABRISI:2:45/r14.claim: The Imams interpret patience as fasting, which curbs greed and desire; prayer recalls God's reward, reduces worldly attachment and leadership-seeking, and instills humility.
TABRISI:2:45/r14.anchor: عن أئمتنا ع أن المراد بالصبر الصوم فيكون فائدة الاستعانة به

TABRISI:2:45#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:2:45#2/r1.claim: When troubled, the Prophet would seek help through prayer and fasting; the report has no grading stated.
TABRISI:2:45#2/r1.anchor: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا حزنه أمر استعان بالصلاة والصوم

TABRISI:2:45#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45#2/r2.claim: On the Muslim-address reading, believers seek help in obtaining the promised reward for following the Prophet, or in bearing religious duties by restraining themselves for obedience and from sins and desires.
TABRISI:2:45#2/r2.anchor: ومن قال إنه خطاب للمسلمين قال المراد به استعينوا على تنجز ما وعدته لمن اتبع النبي

TABRISI:2:45#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45#2/r3.claim: Prayer helps through Qur'an recitation, reflection, moral admonition, obedience to commands, and avoidance of prohibitions.
TABRISI:2:45#2/r3.anchor: وبالصلاة لما فيها من تلاوة القرآن والتدبر لمعانيه والاتعاظ بمواعظه

TABRISI:2:45#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45#2/r4.claim: Another explanation says patience is the greatest act of the heart and prayer the greatest act of the limbs, so God commands help through both.
TABRISI:2:45#2/r4.anchor: ليس في أفعال القلوب أعظم من الصبر ولا في أفعال الجوارح أعظم من الصلاة

TABRISI:2:45#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45#2/r5.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABRISI:2:45#2/r5.claim: Al-Ṣādiq advises anyone struck by worldly grief to make ablution, pray two rakʿas in the mosque, and supplicate, citing this verse; no grading is stated.
TABRISI:2:45#2/r5.anchor: وروي عن الصادق ع أنه قال: ما يمنع أحدكم إذا دخل عليه غم من غموم الدنيا أن يتوضأ

TABRISI:2:45#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45#2/r6.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
TABRISI:2:45#2/r6.claim: Most exegetes take the pronoun ‘it’ to refer to prayer, the dominant and superior of the two practices; prayer is singled out because it is nearer, more important, universally obligatory, and emphasized.
TABRISI:2:45#2/r6.anchor: أحدها: أنها عائد إلى الصلاة لأنها الأغلب والأفضل وهو قول أكثر المفسرين

TABRISI:2:45#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45#2/r7.claim: A second grammatical explanation takes the singular pronoun to refer to both patience and prayer, as singular pronouns can follow two coordinated nouns; 62:11 supplies an example.
TABRISI:2:45#2/r7.anchor: والآخر: أن المراد الاثنان وإن كان اللفظ واحدا ويشهد لذلك قوله تعالى

TABRISI:2:45#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45#2/r8.claim: Poetry offers examples of a singular verb or pronoun following two coordinated subjects, supporting a singular pronoun for both patience and prayer.

TABRISI:2:45#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45#3/r1.claim: Another interpretation takes ‘it’ to mean seeking help, understood from the command ‘seek help’; a poetic example similarly uses the adjective to imply its abstract noun.
TABRISI:2:45#3/r1.anchor: وثانيها: أنه عائد إلى الاستعانة يعني أن الاستعانة بهما لكبيرة

TABRISI:2:45#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45#3/r2.speaker: الأصم
TABRISI:2:45#3/r2.claim: Al-Aṣamm suggests an omitted antecedent such as responding to the Prophet.
TABRISI:2:45#3/r2.anchor: وهو الإجابة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الأصم

TABRISI:2:45#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45#3/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:2:45#3/r3.claim: Abū Muslim suggests that the pronoun refers to this offense, one of several possible omitted antecedents.
TABRISI:2:45#3/r3.anchor: أو هذه الخطيئة عن أبي مسلم

TABRISI:2:45#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45#3/r4.claim: The omitted-antecedent proposals are weak because their referents have not been mentioned in the context.
TABRISI:2:45#3/r4.anchor: وهذه الوجوه الأخيرة كلها ضعيفة لأنها لم يجر لها ذكر

TABRISI:2:45#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45#3/r5.speaker: الحسن وغيره
TABRISI:2:45#3/r5.claim: They explain kabīra as heavy or burdensome; anything difficult for the soul is called ‘large’ by metaphor from the weight it bears.

TABRISI:2:45#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45#3/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:45#3/r6.claim: The humble find prayer unburdensome because they have habituated themselves to it; they do not mind losing status if they gain faith.
TABRISI:2:45#3/r6.anchor: فإنهم قد وطنوا أنفسهم على فعلها وعودوها إياها فلا يثقل عليهم

TABRISI:2:45#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45#3/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:2:45#3/r7.claim: Mujāhid identifies the humble as believers: knowing the reward makes prayer light, as someone accepts bitter medicine for the cure it brings.
TABRISI:2:45#3/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد أراد بالخاشعين المؤمنين فإنهم إذا علموا ما يحصل لهم من الثواب بفعلها لم يثقل عليهم ذلك

TABRISI:2:45#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:45#3/r8.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:45#3/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the humble as those who fear God.

THALABI:v1p188/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p188/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p188/r4.claim: One explanation makes the feminine pronoun refer to prayer, the more prominent of patience and prayer, as pronouns can follow the dominant member of a pair.
THALABI:v1p188/r4.anchor: وإنها لكبيرة [عليهما ولكنه كنى عن الأغلب وهو الصلاة كقوله] : والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها

THALABI:v1p188/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p188/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p188/r5.claim: Another explanation takes the feminine singular distributively: each of patience and prayer is difficult, like Mary and Jesus each being a sign.
THALABI:v1p188/r5.anchor: وإنها واحد منهما، أراد بأن كل خصلة منهما لكبيرة

THALABI:v1p188/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p188/r6.speaker: الشاعر
THALABI:v1p188/r6.claim: An unnamed poet’s singular nalahu means whoever attains either quality, supporting a distributive reading of the pronoun.
THALABI:v1p188/r6.anchor: حسن من علم يزينه حلم … ومن ناله قد فاز بالفرج أي من نال كل واحد منهما

THALABI:v1p188/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p188/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p188/r7.claim: A further view returns the pronoun to prayer because patience is included in prayer; the singular in ‘they please him’ likewise reflects the Prophet’s approval being included in God’s.
THALABI:v1p188/r7.anchor: وقيل: رد الهاء الى الصلاة لأن الصبر داخل في الصلاة كقوله: والله ورسوله أحق أن يرضوه

THALABI:v1p188/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p188/r8.speaker: حسان
THALABI:v1p188/r8.claim: Hassan’s poem uses the singular verb ya‘as to refer to youth, which includes black hair, supporting a singular pronoun for a collective pair.
THALABI:v1p188/r8.anchor: وقال الشاعر وهو حسان: إن شرخ الشباب والشعر الأسود

THALABI:v1p188/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p188/r9.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
THALABI:v1p188/r9.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl says the pronoun refers to seeking help itself: seeking help through patience and prayer is burdensome except for the humble.
THALABI:v1p188/r9.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل: رد الكناية إلى الاستعانة، معناه: وأن الاستعانة بالصبر والصلاة لكبيرة

THALABI:v1p188/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p188/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p188/r10.claim: Thalabi says the humble are believers.

THALABI:v1p188/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p188/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p188/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says the humble are those who pray.

THALABI:v1p188/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p188/r12.speaker: الوراق
THALABI:v1p188/r12.claim: Al-Warraq says the humble are worshippers who obey.

THALABI:v1p188/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p188/r13.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
THALABI:v1p188/r13.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan says the humble are those who are submissive.

THALABI:v1p188/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p188/r14.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v1p188/r14.claim: Hasan says the humble are those who fear God.

THALABI:v1p188/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p188/r15.speaker: الزجاج
THALABI:v1p188/r15.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines the humble person as one whose appearance shows lowliness and submission, deriving the word from the desolate, subdued state of a house.
THALABI:v1p188/r15.anchor: قال الزجاج: الخاشع الذي يرى أثر الذل والخنوع عليه، وكخشوع الدار بعد الإقواء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p451/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p451/r1.speaker: أبو عبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p451/r1.claim: Abu Ubayd derives sabr from restraint, explaining expressions for holding a killer, a person held for execution, self-restraint and an oath imposed by keeping someone there; Antara's verse illustrates restraint.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p451/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيد (¬1): أصل الصبر الحبس، وكل من حبس شيئا فقد صبره،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p451/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p451/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p451/r2.claim: Seek help through patience in performing obligations, avoiding forbidden acts, bearing harm and calamities, and fighting enemies; prayer helps because it restrains indecency and wrongdoing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p451/r2.anchor: ومعنى الآية: استعينوا بالصبر على أداء الفرائض واجتناب المحارم واحتمال الأذى وجهاد العدو وعلى المصائب والصلاة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p451/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p451/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p451/r3.claim: Mujahid interprets patience here as fasting; Ramadan is called the month of patience and the fasting person a patient one.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p451/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الصبر في هذه الآية الصوم، ويقال لشهر رمضان شهر الصبر، وللصائم صابر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r1.speaker: الحسن، الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r1.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak explain kabira as heavy or burdensome.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r2.claim: The underlying analogy is that what is big is heavy to carry, so anything psychologically difficult can be called big, as in the verse about what is urged on polytheists.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r2.anchor: والأصل في ذلك أن ما يكبر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r3.speaker: المؤرج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r3.claim: Al-Muarrij says the singular pronoun refers to prayer, the dominant, best and most important of the two; examples show a predicate agreeing with one of two named items.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r3.anchor: وقال: {وإذا رأوا تجارة أو لهوا انفضوا إليها} [الجمعة: 11]، هذا قول المؤرج (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r4.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash says the pronoun applies distributively to each of patience and prayer, as the verse calls Mary and her son a sign while meaning each individually.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r4.anchor: وقال الأخفش (¬3): الكناية راجعة إلى كل واحد منهما، أراد وإن كل خصلة منها لكبيرة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r5.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r5.claim: An unnamed poet's line is cited as evidence for a singular predicate applying to both coordinated terms distributively.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r5.anchor: كقوله: {وجعلنا ابن مريم وأمه آية} [المؤمنون: 50]، أراد كل واحد منهما قال الشاعر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r6.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r6.claim: One explanation returns the pronoun to prayer because patience is included within prayer, as the Prophet's pleasure is included in God's pleasure.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r6.anchor: وقيل: رد الهاء إلى الصلاة، لأن الصبر داخل في الصلاة، كقوله: {والله ورسوله أحق أن يرضوه}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r7.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r7.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl says the pronoun refers to seeking help, since the command استعينوا implies that verbal noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r7.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل: رد الكناية إلى الاستعانة، لأن (استعينوا) يدل على المصدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r8.claim: Arabic can name two things and predicate only one, relying on that predicate to imply the other; the author illustrates this with Quranic examples and a poem contrasting viewpoints.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p452/r8.anchor: والأصل في هذا وأمثاله أن العرب تذكر شيئين، ثم تخبر عن أيهما شاءت، فتكتفي بالخبر عن أحدهما عن الثاني،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r1.claim: Khushu' originally means stillness; the verse says voices become still before the Merciful.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r2.claim: A wall described as khashi' has collapsed and become level with the ground; al-Nabigha's verse illustrates the usage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r2.anchor: ويقال: جدار خاشع، إذا تداعى واستوى مع الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r3.claim: A report describes the Kaaba as still upon the water, illustrating the same basic sense of khushu'.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r3.anchor: ومنه الحديث (كانت الكعبة خشعة على الماء)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r4.claim: The word extends to land that stays dry and does not sprout, a meaning illustrated by the verse about barren-looking earth receiving rain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r4.anchor: فقيل: خشعت الأرض، إذا لم تمطر، فلم تهتز

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r5.claim: Other extensions describe a hump losing fat and drooping, eyes lowered without glancing, and a submissive worshipper whose stillness reflects obedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r5.anchor: وخشع السنام، إذا ذهب شحمه وتطأطأ شرفه. وخشعت الأبصار، إذا سكنت ونظرت في الأرض من غير التفات.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r6.speaker: أصحاب المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r6.claim: All forms of worship are covered by patience, meaning steadfastness in them; prayer is singled out to emphasize its distinction, as fruit, palm and pomegranate and angels, messengers, Gabriel and Michael are singled out.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r6.anchor: قال المفسرون وأصحاب المعاني: إن (¬6) جميع العبادات داخلة تحت قوله:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r7.claim: If patience means fasting, fasting and prayer answer barriers to Islam: greed and fear of losing food or leadership; fasting curbs greed, while prayer brings humility and removes arrogance and status-seeking.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r7.anchor: وعلى قول من يقول: الصبر هو الصوم (¬1)، فإنما خص الصوم والصلاة، لأن القوم إنما كان يمنعهم عن الإسلام الشره وخوف ذهاب مأكلتهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r8.claim: The intended prayer is prayer joined with belief in Muhammad, which was difficult for unbelievers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r8.anchor: وأريد بالصلاة الصلاة التي معها الإيمان بحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنها كانت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r9.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r9.claim: Most scholars say the address is to the People of the Book, while its instruction remains proper for all worshippers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r9.anchor: وعند أكثر أهل العلم أن الآية خطاب لأهل الكتاب (¬8)، وهو مع ذلك أدب لجميع العباد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r10.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r10.claim: Some say the address is to Muslims, who are told to seek God's pleasure, reward and Paradise through patient observance of obligations; the author says the People of the Book reading is clearer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p455/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم: يرجع هذا القول إلى خطاب المسلمين فأمروا أن يستعينوا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r3.claim: Greed, fear of losing livelihood, and love of leadership kept them from Islam, so God commanded fasting and prayer.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r3.anchor: لأنهم إنما كان يمنعهم عن الإسلام الشره، وخوف ذهاب مأكلتهم، وحب الرياسة،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r4.claim: Fasting removes greed, while prayer produces humility and removes arrogance; the intended prayer is joined with belief in Muhammad.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r4.anchor: فأمروا بالصوم الذي يذهب الشره، وبالصلاة التي تورث الخشوع، وتنفي الكبر،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r5.claim: Patience means fasting; prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing, and seeking help through them is burdensome except for the humble, who are settled in obedience.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r5.anchor: يعني بالصوم، { والصلاة } لأنها تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر { وإنها لكبيرة } لثقيلة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r6.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r6.claim: An alternative view takes this as a return to addressing Muslims, telling them to seek God's approval and Paradise through patient observance of obligations and prayer.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم: رجع بهذا القول إلى خطاب المسلمين، فأمرهم أن يستعينوا على ما يطلبونه

BURHAN:v3p127/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p127/r1.speaker: قتادة
BURHAN:v3p127/r1.claim: A preceding, context-truncated report from Qatada identifies the referents as angels; al-Zarkashi says the antecedent already mentioned fits better.
BURHAN:v3p127/r1.anchor: ونقل عن قتادة قال هم الملائكة والأشبه أن يأتي هنا بما سبق

BURHAN:v3p127/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p127/r6.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v3p127/r6.claim: The pronoun إنّها may refer to prayer as the nearer noun, to the understood act of seeking help, or to both with the first term omitted.
BURHAN:v3p127/r6.anchor: فقيل الضمير للصلاة لأنها أقرب المذكورين وقيل أعاده على المعنى وهو الاستعانة

QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r13.claim: Patience is restraining the soul from familiar comforts, while prayer is presenting oneself for connection; inwardly patience leaves other-than-God and prayer abides in the unseen presence.

QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r14.speaker: النبي
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r14.claim: A transmitted report says that when God manifests Himself to a thing, it becomes humble; such manifestation makes what people endure light and easy.
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r14.anchor: إن الله تعالى إذا تجلى لشيء خشع له

QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r15.claim: Sustained obedience brings the burden of effort, whereas witnessing divine disclosures, by realization, brings complete union and lasting nearness.

QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r16.claim: The servant asks God to help him endure with Him and to preserve his prayer, so unveilings and awe do not absorb him and prevent service.
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r16.anchor: ويقال استعينوا بي على الصبر معي

QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r17.claim: God’s easing of overwhelming states during unveiling lets the servant resume the duties of separation; this is a great divine favor.
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r17.anchor: وإن تخفيف سطوات الوجود على القلب في أوان الكشف

BURHAN:v4p240/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p240/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p240/r2.claim: Illa can follow an affirmative form whose meaning carries an implicit negation, or a statement that is true only with the exception; this differs from the false reading of ضربت إلا زيدا.
BURHAN:v4p240/r2.anchor: فان إلا ما دخلت بعد لفظ الايجاب إلا لتاويل ما سبق إلا بالنفي

BURHAN:v4p30/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p30/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p30/r2.claim: When two antecedents appear, a pronoun most often returns to the second, usually because it is nearer; in وقدره منازل, proximity and the moon’s role in reckoning months both support that choice.
BURHAN:v4p30/r2.anchor: قد يذكر شيئان ويعاد الضمير على احدهما ثم الغالب كونه للثاني

DAMGHANI:v1p157/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p157/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p157/r3.claim: Khushūʿ can mean humility; the verse says the duty is difficult except for the humble.
DAMGHANI:v1p157/r3.anchor: يعني المتواضعين الثاني : الخشوع يعني الخوف فذلك قوله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p276/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p276/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p276/r6.anchor: والرابع : التواضع . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba groups examples where number or pronouns do not repeat each coordinated item, including singular predicates for paired terms.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r1.anchor: وقال: عن اليمين وعن الشمال قعيد

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r1.claim: This imperative coordinates with the preceding commands, although intervening clauses interrupt it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r1.anchor: هذه الجملة الأمرية عطف على ما قبلها من الأوامر، ولكن اعترض بينها بهذه الجمل

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r2.claim: استعينوا derives from استعونوا; the sīn marks seeking, with the form discussed under نستعين.

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r3.claim: بالصبر attaches to استعينوا with باء of instrument or cause; the sought aid is omitted to generalize it; استعين may govern directly or by باء, which may also mean being accompanied by patience.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r3.anchor: والباء للاستعانة أو للسببية، والمستعان عليه محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r4.claim: الصبر means holding oneself through hardship; قتل فلان صبرا and a poem about the field of death illustrate it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r4.anchor: والصبر: الحبس على المكروه، ومنه: " قتل فلان صبرا "

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r5.claim: إنها is إن with its noun and predicate; the pronoun may refer to prayer, foremost in importance, though al-Samīn questions the analogy to 62:11 because أو takes a singular pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r5.anchor: والضمير في " إنها " قيل: يعود على الصلاة وإن تقدم شيئان

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r6.claim: Other proposed antecedents are the assistance implied by the verb or worship implied by patience and prayer.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r6.anchor: وقيل: يعود على الاستعانة المفهومة من الفعل نحو

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r7.claim: A further view makes the singular pronoun refer to patience and prayer together; al-Samīn rejects this.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو عائد على الصبر والصلاة، وإن كان بلفظ المفرد، وهذا ليس بشيء

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r8.claim: Another analysis elides a pronoun for the first coordinated matter, understood from the second, as in the cited line about youth and hair.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#3/r8.anchor: وقيل: حذف من الأول لدلالة الثاني عليه، وتقديره: وإنه لكبير

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#4/r1.claim: This is an exceptive construction with an implied negative: the practice is not easy or light except for the humble; على الخاشعين attaches to كبيرة as difficulty.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#4/r1.anchor: وجاز ذلك وإن كان الكلام مثبتا لأنه في قوة المنفي، أي

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#4/r2.claim: خشوع means submissiveness and originates in softness or ease; خشعة is a low soft dune, as in a report that land was soft over water, and al-Nābigha's خاشع suggests abasement.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#4/r2.anchor: والخشوع: الخضوع، وأصله اللين والسهولة، ومنه " الخشعة " للرملة المتطامنة

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#4/r3.claim: Some distinguish خضوع as bodily submission alone, while خشوع includes body, voice, and sight and is broader.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#4/r3.anchor: فقال: الخضوع في البدن خاصة، والخشوع في البدن والصوت والبصر فهو أعم منه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#3/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#3/r8.claim: In 2:45 the pronoun and closing return to prayer because the preceding context commands it; in 2:153 the close turns to patience because the following verses discuss martyrdom, trials, and the patient response in 2:156.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#3/r8.anchor: فلما كان السياق في الموطن الأول عن الصلاة، أعاد الضمير عليها وختم الآية بها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r2.claim: The command is to seek God’s help with one’s needs.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r3.claim: Seek help by joining patience with prayer, enduring its duties, hardships, sincerity, attentiveness, and reverence before God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r3.anchor: أي بالجمع بينهما وان تصلوا صابرين على تكاليف الصلاة محتملين لمشاقها وما يجب فيها من إخلاص القلب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r4.claim: Alternatively, patience means enduring calamities and turning to prayer when they occur.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r4.anchor: أو واستعينوا على البلايا والنوائب بالصبر عليها والالتجاء إلى الصلاة عند وقوعها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r5.claim: When a matter troubled the Prophet, he resorted to prayer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r5.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( إذا حزبه امر فزع إلى الصلاة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r6.claim: When Ibn Abbas learned during travel that his brother Qutham had died, he said the return formula, stepped aside, prayed two rakʿas, then recited this verse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه نعي إليه اخوه قثم وهو في سفر فاسترجع وتنحى عن الطريق فصلى ركعتين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r7.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r7.claim: Some identify patience with fasting, since it restrains a person from food and drink; Ramadan is called the month of patience.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r7.anchor: وقيل الصبر الصوم لأنه حبس عن المفطرات ومنه قيل لشهر رمضان شهر الصبر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r8.claim: Prayer may mean supplication: seek help in hardship through patience and earnest prayer to God for its removal.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r8.anchor: ويجوز ان يراد بالصلاة الدعاء وان يستعان على البلايا بالصبر والالتجاء إلى الدعاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r1.claim: The pronoun may refer to prayer or seeking help, or more broadly to all commands and prohibitions from “Remember My favor” through “seek help.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r1.anchor: الضمير للصلاة أو للاستعانة ويجوز ان يكون لجميع الأمور التى أمر بها بنو اسرائيل ونهوا عنها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r2.claim: Kabīra means difficult and burdensome, as in saying an affair weighs heavily on someone.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r2.anchor: لشاقة ثقيلة من قولك كبر علي هذا الأمر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r3.claim: The same usage appears in the statement that what the Prophet calls people to weighs heavily on polytheists.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r3.anchor: ﴿ كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه ﴾ الشورى 13

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r4.claim: Prayer is not burdensome to the humble because they anticipate the reward stored for those who endure its demands.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r4.anchor: لأنهم يتوقعون ما ادخر للصابرين على متاعبها فتهون عليهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r7.claim: For those who lack certainty about recompense and hope for reward, prayer is sheer hardship, as for hypocrites and showoffs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r7.anchor: واما من لم يوقن بالجزاء ولم يرج الثواب كانت عليه مشقة خالصة فثقلت عليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r8.claim: The Prophet said prayer was made the comfort of his eyes, and he would ask Bilal to refresh them with it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r8.anchor:
قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
35 ( وجعلت قرة عيني في الصلاة )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r9.claim: Khushūʿ is humility and stillness; the related word for a low patch of sand reflects its sunken form.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r9.anchor: والخشوع الإخبات والتطامن ومنه الخشعة للرملة المتطامنة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r10.claim: Khuḍūʿ means gentleness and submission; the idiom “she softened her speech” illustrates it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162#2/r10.anchor: واما الخضوع فاللين والانقياد ومنه خضعت بقولها اذا لينته
